#4186. Best Cars for Snow

Snow performance is all about tires and clearance, so we selected the top-rated new vehicles that come from the factory with snow-rated rubber.

When discussing a car’s performance in the snow, it all comes down to tires and clearance. Tires are the only part of your vehicle that makes contact with the road, so the rubber mounted on your car is the number-one determiner of how much grip you’ll have while accelerating, turning, or braking on slippery surfaces such as snow and ice. All-wheel drive may help you get going in the snow, but it doesn’t help you stop.

So, when selecting this list of best vehicles for snow, we included only top-rated models that come standard from the factory with tires rated for severe snow service. These tires are marked with the all-important three-peak mountain snowflake icon (3PMSF). This icon is found on either all-weather tires or all-terrain tires that have been tested and are capable of at least 110 percent of the traction of a reference all-season tire. Not every all-terrain tire carries this marking.

It’s also important to mention that any car with winter tires would be our preferred method of transportation in snowy conditions. If you don’t want to pony up for one of these SUVs or trucks with their often pricey optional off-road packages that include the 3PMSF tires, consider outfitting a different vehicle with winter tires. Check out our Winter Tire Buying Guide for advice on which tires to choose.

The CX-50 is one of our favorite compact SUVs, and it offers a rugged-looking trim level called the Meridian Edition. This version comes with snow-rated all-terrain tires no matter whether you choose the naturally aspirated 2.5 S Meridian Edition or the more powerful Turbo Meridian Edition.

Tire: General Grabber A/T or Pirelli Scorpion XTM A/T

If you’re not willing to go all out for the Raptor version of the F-150 found later on this list, this popular pickup truck also offers a lesser off-road trim level that also comes with snow-rated tires. The F-150 Tremor doesn’t have the upgraded engine or suspension from the Raptor, but it does have style upgrades and other modifications compared with the standard F-150. There are two factory tire choices, either General or Pirelli, but both have the 3PMSF icon.

Many versions of the Ram 1500 pickup offer an Off-Road Group option package that includes Falken Wildpeak all-terrain tires in various sizes, all of which have the 3PMSF icon. Ironically enough, the Ram’s most off-road-oriented versions—the Rebel, RHO, and TRX—also have all-terrain tires, but not ones specifically rated for snow.

The GX is closely related to the Toyota Land Cruiser and is the most off-road-ready SUV in the Lexus lineup. To get snow-rated tires from the factory, you have to opt for the Overtrail model, which comes with all-terrain tires and other upgrades meant to improve the GX’s performance in the dirt and other types of off-road terrain. It has an impressive 9.8 inches of ground clearance.

Ford Ranger Raptor, Ford F-150 Raptor, Ford Bronco Raptor

Tire: BFGoodrich All-Terrain T/A K02 and K03

The BFGoodrich K0 series of off-road tires is well regarded among off-road enthusiasts. Ford’s Raptor off-road pickups, the Ranger and F-150, come with the latest K03 tires, while the Bronco Raptor SUV comes with K02s. We’re fans of all of these high-performance 4x4s, but the Ranger Raptor is our favorite of the bunch due to its smaller size, lower base price, and subdued styling.

Subaru has offered standard all-wheel drive on nearly all of its models for quite a while now, which has earned it a reputation for all-weather performance. But not every Subaru comes with tires optimized for snow. Only the Wilderness version of the Outback mid-size SUV comes with Yokohama Geolandar All-Terrain tires that carry this rating. (The Forester Wilderness and Crosstrek Wilderness also have these tires, but those models don’t rate as high in our testing.)

Mercedes-Benz G550 with G Professional Package

No, you probably don’t need a G-wagen to traipse through a few inches of snow to get to the grocery store. But this highly capable SUV has become a style icon for its distinctive aesthetic, and for good reason. The most capable version of the G-class is the G550 with the G Professional package, which adds all-terrain tires, a roof rack, a bull bar on the front, and other off-road upgrades.

The Mustang Mach-E compact electric SUV is one of the few vehicles you can get from the factory with all-weather tires, in this case the Michelin CrossClimate2. #4185. Battlefield 6 may have actually done it: beaten Call of Duty

Battlefield 6 sales are setting all kinds of records, but one in particular has long eluded the Battlefield series.

If you’ve been paying any attention to the shooter market these past few months, you won’t be surprised to learn that Battlefield 6 has been an unprecedented success for EA, and the Battlefield series as a whole.

The game managed to sell over 7 million units at launch, climbing to the top of the charts anywhere you look, including setting new series concurrent player records on Steam. Thanks to new data, we now better understand the true scale of this launch.

The latest Circana report, which looks at game and hardware sales in the United States, has arrived. This iteration covers the month of October, which is when Battlefield 6 was released.

Battlefield 6 was the top-selling game across all platforms during October - which isn’t surprising. It has overtaken NBA 2K26 to become 2025’s best-selling game year-to-date, making it the best-selling Battlefield game ever.

In October alone, the game sold more than the lifetime sales of Battlefield 1, previously the best-selling entry in the franchise.

Battlefield 6 even set records beyond just its own series, having now produced the highest single-month dollar sales (physical and digital) total for any full game released in the last three years. The previous record holder was 2022’s Modern Warfare 2.

November’s report, which is set to arrive midway through December, will show, once and for all, whether Battlefield 6 has been able to overtake Black Ops 7. With one exception, Call of Duty games have, for more than a decade, topped the best-selling year-to-date chart. Regardless of the quality of the individual titles, or the competition in any given year, nothing has been able to shake that dominance.

Given all this momentum, Battlefield 6 has a shot at dethroning Call of Duty this year, beating Black Ops 7 to become the year’s best-seller. You never want to count out the sheer popularity of Call of Duty among casual players, however, which is what’s going to make December’s report all the more interesting.

#4184. PUBG's extraction shooter spin-off, Black Budget, is finally going to be playable next month

The most interesting development in the PUBG universe, PUBG: Black Budget, is almost ready to show itself off to a wider group of players.

You’d be forgiven for not remembering PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction off-shoot of the original battle royale shooter, PUBG. Black Budget has been sort of floating around the internet for months, but Krafton never really committed to revealing core details about the game, or when players will actually get to play it.

This changes today, as the publisher - along with the game’s developer, PUBG Studios, have finally lifted the lid off the upcoming shooter.

Black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter. Squads of players infiltrate a mysterious island trapped in a time loop. There’s a bit of a STALKER element here with anomalies and various, unpredictable environmental shifts.

Coli, the island in question, hides a research facility that holds secrets and artefacts, which is what players will be attempting to extract. This is very much a PvPvE shooter, though PUBG Studios says the focus will be on exploration and discovery, rather than constant combat.

The game’s first set of closed alpha tests is set for December. The first takes place December 12-14, and another is scheduled for December 19-21. That’s six days across two weeks, with the test only being available on PC. Both sessions will be open to players in North America, Europe, and Asia.

As it usually works with these sorts of tets on Steam, the game’s Steam page has a link where you can request access. If granted, you’ll be able to find the closed alpha in your library and download it when the time comes.

Though this is a closed test, Krafton confirmed that players will be able to capture and livestream their gameplay. In fact, watching content creators might be how you get access, as Black Budget is going to have a Twitch Drops event running alongside those sessions.

When I played Arc Raiders prior to its launch, I likened its tense and uncertain atmosphere to that of the early days of PUBG, so it’s going to be very interesting to see what actual PUBG does with the extraction shooter premise.

So far, it sounds like it’s going to be doing its own thing, leaning more into the adventure side of the subgenre, but we’ll have to see how it all shakes out when the tests start. Indeed, the BR-like constantly shrinking circle sounds like it could be a game-changing twist.

#4183. The Tesla Cybertruck Is America’s Fastest-Selling Used Truck

EVs are selling faster than gas vehicles, with the Cybertruck leading used trucks and 16 EVs landing among the 25 fastest-selling models.

Even though it was recently canceled, the Tesla Cybertruck is the number-one-selling used car in America. That’s based on analysis of over 1.1 million used-vehicle sales from October 2026 by iSeeCars.com. It includes the fastest-selling trucks and the 25 fastest- and slowest-selling vehicles overall.

In fact, EVs take 25 percent less time to sell than gas vehicles in the used market, and among those EVs there are three Teslas in the top 25, including the Cybertruck, Model 3, and Model Y. And 16 of the 25 fastest-selling used vehicles are EVs.

“Why do so many electric vehicles, including the recently canceled Cybertruck, sell so rapidly on the used market? The combination of sustained high fuel prices and a dramatic drop in market value essentially ‘flips the script’ on EVs when they transition from new to used status,” said iSeeCars Executive Analyst Karl Brauer.

Here are some numbers: EVs average 45.6 days on the market compared with 54.5 days for hybrids and 61.0 days for gasoline vehicles, according to iSeeCars. Those 45.6 days are 15.4 days less than gasoline vehicles and 8.9 days less than hybrids. The overall industry average is 59.5 days. Used EVs spend 25.2 percent less time on the market than gasoline vehicles, while hybrids spend 10.7 percent less time on the market than gasoline models.

See all results for new 2026 Tesla Cybertruck for sale near 06010

And despite the fact that many electric pickup trucks have recently been axed, EV pickups in general are particularly well represented among the fastest-selling used trucks, the study says. Four of the top 10 trucks are electric, and three of them rank among the top four fastest-selling pickups.

The Tesla Cybertruck leads the rankings at 39.1 days on the market, selling in 26.4 fewer days than the average used pickup. The Ford Maverick hybrid ranks second at 43.3 days, followed by the fully electric Rivian R1T at 45.2 days and the Ford F-150 Lightning at 47.4 days.

Gasoline-powered trucks account for five of the top 10 positions, led by the Toyota Tacoma in fifth place at 50.1 days. The Ford Maverick hybrid ranks second, outperforming all electric trucks except the Cybertruck.

However, not every electric pickup sells quickly. The Chevrolet Silverado EV ranks last among all 24 trucks, averaging 107.5 days on the market. That’s 68.4 days longer than the Cybertruck and 42.0 days longer than the average truck.

EVs also perform strongly in the broader used market, per iSeeCars, where they claim 16 of the 25 fastest-selling model rankings.

The Audi A4 Allroad is the fastest-selling used vehicle overall, averaging just over a month on the market, or 33.7 days, followed by the Lexus RX 450h+ plug-in hybrid at 35.0 days and Audi Q4 Sportback e-tron at 36.3 days.

See all results for new 2026 Tesla Cybertruck for sale near 06010

Electric vehicles occupy six of the top 10 positions, including the Audi Q4 Sportback e-tron, Audi Q6 e-tron, Hyundai Ioniq 5, Lexus RZ 300e, Kia EV9, and BMW i5. All six average fewer than 39 days on the market, compared with the overall used vehicle average of 59.5 days.

The Tesla Cybertruck ranks 16th among all used vehicles, averaging 39.1 days, while the Tesla Model 3 ranks 18th at 39.5 days and Tesla Model Y ranks 24th at 39.8 days. Electric models from Kia, Rivian, Subaru, Toyota, and Volkswagen also appear in the top 25.

What are the slowest sellers on the used car market? The Cadillac Escalade IQ is the slowest-selling vehicle in the study, averaging 134.3 days on the market, more than twice the overall industry average. The Ford Escape plug-in hybrid ranks second at 127.3 days, followed by the Lincoln Corsair hybrid at 114.0 days.

The Silverado EV ranks fourth at 107.5 days, making it both the slowest-selling electric pickup and one of the slowest-selling used vehicles overall.

Two additional electric vehicles appear among the slowest-selling models: the electric Dodge Charger, averaging 98.2 days, and the GMC Hummer EV SUV, averaging 84.9 days.

“There’s clearly a big shift from new to used status for electric vehicles, especially when fuel prices have remained elevated for several months,” said Brauer. “Used shoppers are all about value, which normally plays against electric vehicles. But when consumers see their fuel budget jump 20 to 30 percent, the value of not visiting a gas station leads straight to used EVs.”

#4182. Cannabis users develop psychosis years earlier, and the gap grows with age

A major international analysis has found that people who use cannabis experience their first episode of psychosis about two and a half years earlier, on average, than those who do not use the drug. Even more concerning, the difference becomes substantially larger with age, reaching more than six years among people who develop psychosis in their 30s or later.

The findings, published in the journal Biological Psychiatry, come from researchers at UNSW Sydney. They suggest that the potential psychiatric consequences of cannabis use may extend well beyond adolescence and could become more pronounced with prolonged exposure.

Psychosis is a condition in which a person experiences a disruption in their perception of reality. Symptoms can include hallucinations, false beliefs known as delusions, and disturbances in thinking or behavior. It can occur in schizophrenia and several other mental health disorders. Although psychosis most commonly begins during the late teenage years or early adulthood, it can develop at other stages of life. According to Psychosis Australia, up to 3% of adults will experience a diagnosed disorder involving psychosis during their lifetime.

Cannabis Linked to Earlier Psychosis Across Adulthood

To investigate the relationship between cannabis use and the timing of psychosis, researchers at UNSW Medicine analyzed 149 studies involving more than 71,000 participants. Most of the research had been conducted since 2011 in Europe, North America, and Australia, with the majority of studies focusing on people diagnosed with schizophrenia.

The researchers discovered that the difference in the age at which psychosis first appeared varied considerably across age groups.

In studies where the average age of psychosis onset was between 20 and 24, cannabis users experienced their first episode approximately 1.6 years earlier than non-users. That difference widened to 4.43 years in studies involving people whose psychosis emerged in their mid-to-late 20s (25-29).

The largest difference appeared in studies where psychosis developed at age 30 or later. In this group, cannabis users experienced the condition an average of 6.3 years earlier than non-users.

These results suggest that the association between cannabis and earlier psychosis may become stronger as people grow older, potentially reflecting the effects of longer periods of cannabis exposure.

Chief investigator Matthew Large, a psychiatrist and Conjoint Professor at UNSW's School of Clinical Medicine, said the findings raise important questions about the long-term psychiatric effects of cannabis.

"We've tended to focus on the dangers of using cannabis in adolescence, when the brain is still developing, but the risk doesn't disappear once you're in your 20s," Prof. Large said. "What we're seeing suggests a cumulative effect, where harm builds up over time, a bit like alcohol or nicotine."

Interestingly, the analysis did not identify a statistically significant difference in the timing of psychosis between teenage cannabis users and teenagers who did not use cannabis.

However, the researchers cautioned that this finding does not necessarily mean younger cannabis users face no risk. Psychosis rarely develops before the middle teenage years, leaving relatively little opportunity for its onset to shift to an even younger age.

"There may be a biological floor, in that there is only so much earlier that onset can be shifted. In younger groups, strong development, genetic or other psychosis risk factors may dominate, making any cannabis-related age shift harder to detect," Prof. Large said.

The researchers also stressed an important limitation. Because the analysis examined existing observational studies, it cannot establish that cannabis directly causes psychosis or makes the condition begin sooner. Demonstrating such a relationship experimentally would require research that deliberately exposed people to potential psychiatric harm, which would be unethical.

Nevertheless, Prof. Large believes the overall pattern provides meaningful evidence supporting a possible causal connection.

"But the consistency of the evidence, particularly the strong effect in older adults who likely have been using cannabis for longer, does support the theory that cannabis plays a causal role in the timing of psychosis onset, and possibly the onset of some cases among people who would not have otherwise developed psychosis."

New Findings Challenge Assumptions About Cannabis After Age 25

The latest research builds on two earlier investigations into cannabis use and the development of psychosis.

In a smaller 2011 meta-analysis led by Prof. Large, researchers found that psychosis began approximately 2.7 years earlier among cannabis users. A separate 2015 analysis reported that psychosis typically developed 6.3 years after cannabis use began.

However, neither earlier investigation had enough information to determine how the relationship differed across age groups.

By incorporating a much larger body of research, the new analysis allowed scientists to examine how the association changes across different stages of adulthood.

Lead author Carly Stevens, from UNSW's School of Biomedical Sciences, said the findings undermine the idea that avoiding cannabis during adolescence is sufficient to eliminate its potential psychiatric dangers.

"What we've found challenges the assumption that you'll be fine if you wait to smoke weed until your mid-20s; that's just not the case," Ms. Stevens said.

"There's been so much emphasis on adolescents not smoking cannabis, which is important, but we need to broaden the warnings for everyone."

Why Even a Few Years of Delayed Psychosis Matter

Although a difference of two or three years might initially seem relatively small, the researchers emphasized that the timing of psychosis can have profound consequences for a person's future.

The late teenage years and early adulthood are often periods when people complete their education, begin careers, establish relationships, and develop greater independence. Experiencing a serious psychiatric disorder earlier in life can interrupt these important milestones.

"People may miss out on study, job opportunities, travel, and relationships in those years, and treatment can come with physical side effects that can make life harder as well," Ms. Stevens said.

Prof. Large emphasized the potential benefits of reducing or discontinuing cannabis use and the importance of delaying the onset of psychosis wherever possible.

"It's a major illness, which robs you of your shared reality with family, friends and all those around you," he said. "If we can delay psychosis by even a few years, people will be more likely to reach crucial milestones in education and training, and develop strong support networks, which can protect against psychosocial decline."

The potential benefits could also extend to healthcare systems. According to Prof. Large, psychotic disorders account for as much as 3% of health-related spending in developed countries. Preventing or delaying the onset of these conditions could therefore have substantial social and economic benefits.

Scientists Call for Stronger Cannabis Health Warnings

Despite the inability to establish a direct cause-and-effect relationship, the researchers believe their findings provide sufficient justification for stronger warnings about the possible psychiatric consequences of cannabis use.

"We can't run direct experiments, so we have to go with the best evidence available," Prof. Large said. "In my view, the threshold for health warnings about cannabis and psychosis has definitely been met."

One concern is the growing popularity of medical cannabis. Prof. Large said its increasing use as a therapeutic product may encourage some people to assume that it carries little risk.

He has also observed an increasing number of patients receiving treatment for psychosis who had previously been prescribed cannabis for medical conditions where evidence supporting its effectiveness remains limited.

"It's got this therapeutic halo around it, which blinds people to the risk."

Another emerging concern involves cannabis edibles, which can contain elevated concentrations of Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the main compound responsible for the drug's mind altering effects. The availability of products containing higher THC concentrations raises additional questions about possible psychiatric risks.

At the same time, Prof. Large acknowledged that cannabis legalization could create opportunities to reduce harm, even though it would also make cannabis easier to obtain.

Legal regulation could allow governments to establish limits on product potency, improve consumer education, introduce taxation, and require buyers to receive clear information about potential health consequences.

"You could tax it, regulate it, and require people to show they understand the risks before buying," Prof. Large said.

More Research Needed on Long-Term Cannabis Exposure

The researchers say further studies are necessary to understand the biological processes that might explain why the association between cannabis use and earlier psychosis becomes more pronounced with age.

In particular, they want to investigate whether repeated or prolonged cannabis exposure produces cumulative changes that influence when psychotic symptoms emerge.

They also recommend additional research focusing on older cannabis users, an increasingly important population as medical cannabis becomes more common and products containing high concentrations of THC become more widely available.

Another priority is improving how cannabis exposure is measured. The researchers argue that future studies need clearer and more consistent methods for recording cannabis consumption so that findings can be compared more reliably.

Ultimately, the new analysis highlights an important gap in public understanding of cannabis and mental health. While warnings have traditionally concentrated on teenage use, the findings suggest that potential psychiatric risks deserve attention throughout adulthood, particularly among people who continue using cannabis over many years.

#4181. Dragon boy Durin is the star of the show in Genshin Impact's wintry Luna 3 update, launching in early December

Genshin Impact is getting two new characters and a whole host of new content in Version Luna 3, which arrives in under two weeks.

The latest HoYoverse Special Program has brought us big Genshin Impact news. Version Luna 3 has been fully revealed, continuing the Nod-Krai story. The new chapter arrives December 3 across all platforms.

The Moon-Prayer Night is the big in-world festival, marking Dameselette's final night before she sets off for the moon. The new update, of course, introduces new playable characters, one with an interesting mechanic.

The events of this new chapter take place following Rarcher of Solnari’s defeat. The victory has given way to the Moon-Prayer Night celebrations, which brings various stalls to the Nasha Town, alongside a new souvenir stamp book where you can record your memories.

All is not fine, however, as Alice and Nicole Reeyn come bearing some bad news about phantoms appearing across the Nod-Krai region at Teyvat's borders. There’s a mystery to be uncovered here, and your journey to do so won’t be a lonely one.

The highly-anticipated Durin is at last the new playable character. A 5-Star Pyro Sword wielder, Durin can switch between two different forms: one lets him deal damage, while the other is best suited to supporting the team.

Durin was once a dragon, you see, who was later given a human body. This is why he’s able to switch forms. The more powerful, Abyssal-infused form can launch major attacks on single targets to boost his own Vaporize and Melt damage, while his support form reduces enemies’ Elemental Resistance and deals AoE Pyro damage.

Durin’s Story Quest will shed more light on that aspect of his life, and completing it earns you a reward for him. Speaking of quests, completing the Archon Quest will grant you 500 Primogems. As a member of Hexenzirkel, Durin and other characters can gain new powers when you complete more quests in Moon-Prayer Night.

All characters connected to the Hexenzirkel can benefit from certain story quests tied to their abilities. This is a big new addition, and will affect Venti, Klee, Albedo, Mona, Razor, Fischl, and Sucrose - all of whom can become Hexerei characters. This ties into the new Hexerei Secret Rite effect, which will trigger when two or more Hexerei characters are present. The effect boosts the entire party’s combat effectiveness.

The other new character in Luna 3 is Jahoda, a 4-Star Anemo Bow wielder who’s great at healing teammates and absorbing Elements, which she can then use to deal damage. The first phase of Luna 3 will feature Durin and Jahoda, alongside the return of Venti. The second phase sees no new character debuts, but does feature the return of Varesa and Xilonen.

There’s more to get excited about in Luna 3, even if you don’t feel like spending most of your time in Nod-Krai. The Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey event will take you back to Dragonspine, where you’ll find winter-theme minigames appropriate to an update cycle spanning December to January. This is how you can earn the 4-Star Rainbow Serpent's Rain Bow, too.

Beyond that, you can also look forward to the Miliastra Wonderland UGC module getting new updates. The Wonderland Resource Center is where creators can get and share resources through the editing tool.

#4180. The Most Valuable Hot Wheels Cars Ever

We bet this list of 23 little cars with big price tags will make you double-check your personal collection—or start one.

Collecting cars is expensive, time-consuming, and something of a game of patience. Collecting little die-cast cars is mostly just the latter two. However, at the top end of the game, rare and hard-to-find Hot Wheels can command prices that raise eyebrows.

To get a sense of where the market is at right now and where it’s going, we caught up with Hot Wheels uber-collector Bruce Pascal. Pascal has thousands of die-cast cars in his collection, which even extends to the full-size classic hot rod “King T,” which inspired the 1968 Hot Wheels Hot Heap. Together, the collection is worth over a million dollars, and it includes an example of the most valuable Hot Wheels of them all, the one at the bottom of this list.

Before diving in on the spendy stuff, Pascal was quick to note that the Hot Wheels collecting hobby is as broad as it is deep. He notes that while eBay used to be where auction battles raised prices higher, about half of all transactions these days occur on Facebook fan pages, with regular auctions, Deal or No Deal style haggling, and sometimes even other Hot Wheels fans throwing some cash on the table to help someone else lock down a buy of a car that perhaps had sentimental value.

You can find most of these places by identifying your segment of interest in Hot Wheels, whether that's the “Redline” cars of the 1960s and 1970s, “Blackwall later cars,” or just plain typing in “Hot Wheels” for everything. Pascal notes that the vast majority of transactions are for less than $10, so feel free to wheel and deal as you build up your own toy car collection. They’re a lot easier to find parking for than a full-size one. Meantime, here’s a look at the Hot Wheels that fetch the most money when they change hands.

2026 Red Line Club Ferrari F40 - $120–$150

Values of the full-size Ferrari F40 have more than doubled over the past few years, making owning one a multimillion-dollar payout. If you’d invested on a smaller scale, you could have doubled your money too. Mattel’s Red Line Club costs under 10 bucks a year and opens up access to highly detailed die-casts for members only. The RLC F40 debuted in August for $50, and examples are now trading for as much as triple that on eBay. It's not nearly the same money as the 1960s cars, but it shows that anyone can get into the Hot Wheels collecting game.

1974 Magenta Rodger Dodger with White Interior – $3000

First issued in 1974, Rodger Dodgers with a black interior are relatively common; those with the white-colored interior are rare, as pictured here, and are the ones that collectors desire.

The Chevrolet Camaro is probably the most Hot Wheels of Hot Wheels, right out of the gate as one of the original 16 castings produced. Brown over a white interior is among the rarest combinations, although values on these haven't really changed much over the past few years.

Rare Hot Wheels Prototype Camaro Worth $100,000

1972 Pink Superfine Turbine – $3500–$4500

Designed by Larry Wood, the Superfine Turbine design dates from the early 1970s and has remained fairly stable in price recently. Wood joined Hot Wheels back in 1969 and was with the company for 50 years, collaborating with the likes of Ed “Big Daddy” Roth and George Barris.

Another Hot Wheels flight of fancy and designed by Paul Tam, the Open Fire is a stretched-out AMC Gremlin with six wheels and plenty of motor. This little green goblin is rare, but prices have held steady of late.

1969 Red Baron with White Interior – $4500–$5000

With its German helmet theme, the Red Baron incorporates a bit of 1960s biker culture and has been reissued many times. This original one, with the rare white interior, is the collector’s choice.

Datsun’s 240Z got some respect right out of the gate in the early 1970s, but fans had to wait until 1977 for Hot Wheels to get its first imported car model. These have doubled in price since 2019.

A hopped-up Mopar with flames, the Rodger Dodger was built in low quantities with blue paint. The rarity drives the price up, as it has also doubled in value over the years.

1971 Spectraflame Purple Bye Focal – $6000

Bye Focal was Mattel’s term for a range of colors in the 1970s, and this purple was the rarest of them. The twin hood scoops are a nice touch, but this model has an Achilles’ heel where the body will begin to fall apart. That just makes surviving examples more rare.

1969 Cheetah Base with Python Body – $6000

This example is a prototype Hot Wheels, one that escaped into the wild even though it wasn’t meant to. The production model was intended to be called the Python, but the original in-house name was the Cheetah. Since only a handful of cars were built with the early base plate on them, that makes this model valuable.

1968 Pink Beatnik Bandit – $6000 (in package, $20,000)

Based on an Ed Roth hot rod, the Beatnik Bandit was another of the first Sweet Sixteen original Hot Wheels. The casting came in nearly 20 colors, but the pink shade is the rarest and thus the most sought after. Prices have remained pretty steady, though an example still in the original packaging fetched five figures recently.

1970 Red Ferrari 312P with White Interior – $7000

Almost every example of this Ferrari model produced came with a black plastic interior. This casting has the white interior that collectors obsess over finding.

Said to be the very first Hot Wheels to make production, the white version of the original run Custom Camaro was supposedly meant to be a blank canvas for designers. Add flames? Chrome-look paint? By mistake, some of these cars were packaged up and sent out, finding their way to the public.

1971 Red Olds 442 with Black Interior – $8000

Another model unusual for its color combination, the Olds 442 casting almost never came in red over black. It’s rumored that fewer than 15 surviving examples of these cars currently exist.

A relative newcomer to the ultra-collectible Hot Wheels segment, this 917 sprang up the charts thanks to its combo of bright paint and association with Porsche. Even Hot Wheels isn’t immune from the air-cooled Porsche boom.

Everyone loves a Woody wagon, but Hot Wheels didn't make many of them in 1969. Again, rarity drives the price point.

A U.K. import, this AMX was made as part of a sponsorship deal with drag racer Ed Shaver. Hot Wheels made lots of AMX castings, so the critical thing is finding one with the original side decals—and making sure they’re the genuine item.

The actual valuation on this little brown Mopar is actually something of a question mark. It’s rare though the casting was very popular, as Hot Wheels didn’t make many examples with brown paint. However, none have changed hands recently, so the actual auction price for one could be much higher.

1969 Mad Maverick Base on Mighty Maverick – $15,000

Another case of a name change driving a big price boost because of rarity, a copyright issue with rival die-cast company Johnny Lightning meant Mattel had to change the name of the Mad Maverick to the Mighty Maverick. However, a few escaped with the original name.

Considered to be one of the rarest production Redline Hot Wheels, this purple 442 has steadily increased in price recently to break into the top five of the most valuable Hot Wheels. It was made exclusively in Mattel’s Hong Kong facilities for just a single year.

#4179. Battlefield 6 kicks off its first free trial post the Black Ops 7 launch to twist that knife

Activision has done its own fair share of Battlefield 6 counterprogramming prior to that game's release, and EA is here to repay the favour with Black Ops 7.

Even if you don’t care about the rivalries between the top multiplayer first-person shooters series, it’s hard to ignore how much EA wanted to stick it to Call of Duty this year with Battlefield 6.

Activision saw that coming early enough that it ran multiple free weekends around major moments for EA’s game, including its launch, seemingly in an effort to capture some of those players and keep them away from BF6.

Both Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 have now launched, and though exact sales figures may never be detrmined (though EA did announce 7 million sold in the first week), it’s very clear at this point from every metric we can see that BF6 came out on top this year.

The recent Black Ops 7 launch clearly hasn’t made many people happy, so just like Activision made Black Ops 6 free to play at BF6’s launch, EA has now done the same with its own game. The Battlefield 6 free trial, which was announced last week, is just an hour away at the time of this writing.

This is the first trial for the core game, and it arrives some six weeks after Battlefield 6 officialy launched, and four weeks following the release of the free-to-play Battlefield Redsec, which has battle royale and other components.

Beyond all the drama surrounding the two rival shooter franchises, the Battlefield 6 trial is itself pretty straightfoward, and is notably nowhere near as genrous as some of the Call of Duty ones we’ve seen recently.

The trial goes live today at 4am PT, 7am ET, 12pm GMT across all platforms, and will be available for a week; ending Tuesday, December 2. It includes three core maps: Siege of Cairo, Eastwood, and Blackwell Fields.

Players will have access to four game modes, played on different versions of the same maps. Conquest, Breakthrough, Sabotage, and Team Deathmatch will all be available to choose from, and there don’t appear to be any level or XP limits in the trial.

Unfortunatley, just as the free trial was about to go live, the game got hit with a major matchmaking outage that took down all matchmaking in the core game, leaving Redsec unaffected.

Hopefully EA can resolve this issue before the trial officially kicks off.

#4178. Stellantis Exiting the WEC and Formula E to Focus on New Hi-Po Cars

Rather than spend millions on factory-backed teams, Stellantis will focus on new-car development and customer-racing support.

Stellantis is preparing its exit from the World Endurance Championship (WEC) and Formula E, but the automaker isn’t giving up on motorsports. In fact, the decision is meant to funnel more energy into making motorsports-focused cars for customers.

The Peugeot 9X8 hypercar is Stellantis’s only factory-backed car in the WEC; that partnership will end at the end of the year. The automaker has a bit more skin in the game in Formula E, where Citroën and Opel each hold two spots on the 24-car grid this season. Both teams will exit Formula E at the end of the season in summer 2027.

By ending its FIA World Championship partnerships, Stellantis says it’ll be able to focus on building motorsports-capable cars for enthusiasts. Employees who currently work in the WEC and Formula E divisions will be retained and reassigned to other areas focused on performance-vehicle development and customer racing. Those reassigned employees will likely pivot to work on high-performance Alfa Romeo and Maserati models, as well as new motorsports-inspired variants for Peugeot, Lancia, and Opel.

Stellantis says it’ll continue to build on its engineering and competition knowledge in customer racing programs—especially rally racing, where several of its brands have deep rally roots. Dismantling factory-backed teams likely frees up the automaker to invest more in smaller collaborations with privateer teams, much like its partnership with PH Sport on the Lancia Corse HF in the World Rally Championship.

The restructuring aligns with Stellantis’s FaSTLAne 2030 plan, which aims to launch more than 100 new and refreshed vehicles by 2030. Reassigning motorsports employees to other areas will undoubtedly help streamline the development process for enthusiast-focused cars to meet the automaker’s ambitious goals.

After all, Ram recently returned to the NASCAR Truck Series for the 2026 season, and Dodge recently announced plans to return to the NASCAR Cup Series for the 2027 season with two Charger-based race cars. A spokesperson provided the following statement: “There are no changes to Stellantis North America motorsports programs.”

#4177. Scientists discover a hidden gut defense that could prevent colon cancer

A common antibody found throughout the digestive tract may provide an unexpected defense against colon cancer. Researchers at Rockefeller University have discovered that these immune molecules help regulate the growth of cells lining the intestine, potentially preventing the uncontrolled cell division that can lead to tumors.

In a study published in Nature, scientists found that mice missing a type of antibody known as immunoglobulin A (IgA) developed more than twice as many colon tumors as mice with normal levels of the antibody. The researchers also uncovered how this protection works. IgA attaches to cells along the intestinal lining and helps prevent them from multiplying too rapidly.

Even more promising, when the team administered IgA orally to mice that lacked the antibody, the animals no longer showed an elevated risk of developing tumors.

"One intriguing aspect of this work is that it shows how a natural defense in the gut restrains the cell division that can lead to cancer," says senior author Daniel Mucida, who leads Rockefeller's Laboratory of Mucosal Immunology. "Most cancer research focuses on trying to destroy a tumor that already exists, but what if we could intervene before tumors form?"

The findings may help explain why people with IgA deficiency, a condition in which the body produces little or none of this antibody, face a greater risk of colorectal cancer. They also offer new insight into how gut bacteria, immune defenses, and intestinal cells work together to influence cancer development, potentially even in people with otherwise healthy immune systems.

Why the Gut Contains So Much of This Antibody

IgA is one of the immune system's most abundant antibodies in the digestive tract, where it provides an important early defense against potentially harmful microbes. Unlike antibodies that recognize a single specific target, IgA can interact with many different kinds of gut bacteria and even certain healthy cells belonging to the body.

Scientists have known for decades that the intestines contain unusually large quantities of IgA. However, the reasons for its abundance, and the full range of functions it performs, have remained incompletely understood.

Mucida's laboratory investigates how the intestine manages two essential but sometimes competing responsibilities. It must defend the body against dangerous microorganisms while allowing nutrients from food to pass into the bloodstream. Earlier research from his team has also helped explain how immune cells in the digestive tract contribute to food intolerances and allergies.

For the new study, Gregory Donaldson, a former postdoctoral researcher at Rockefeller who is now an assistant professor at UCLA, set out to better understand how IgA interacts with intestinal bacteria and whether those interactions might influence the development of colon cancer.

"We know these antibodies bind bacteria and, by doing so, can shape the microbiome," he says. "And because IgA deficiency, which affects about 1 in 500 people in the U.S., is linked to colorectal cancer, I wondered whether these interactions might be relevant to the disease."

The microbiome is the community of microorganisms living in and on the body. In the intestines, these microbes perform important functions related to digestion and immune health, but certain bacteria can also contribute to disease under the wrong conditions.

Missing Gut Antibodies More Than Doubled Colon Tumors

To investigate IgA's protective effects, Donaldson compared mice that could not produce the antibody with mice that had normal IgA levels. Both groups were raised together, allowing the researchers to control for differences in food and exposure to microorganisms.

The results revealed a striking difference. Animals without IgA developed substantially more colorectal tumors than their counterparts, consistent with the increased colorectal cancer risk observed in humans with IgA deficiency.

The association was not limited to a single experimental setup. Researchers observed the same pattern using multiple models of colon cancer, strengthening the evidence that IgA plays a meaningful protective role.

"We found this was true for several different kinds of models of colon cancer, so that was a really convincing effect," says Donaldson.

The team then tested whether replacing the missing antibody could reverse the effect. When mice lacking IgA received oral doses of the antibody, their increased susceptibility to colon tumors disappeared.

This result suggested that IgA does more than simply accompany other protective processes in the intestine. Its presence appears to directly influence conditions that determine whether tumors develop.

Scientists Discover a Natural Brake on Cancer Cell Growth

To understand the mechanism behind this protection, the researchers examined epithelial cells, which form the inner lining of the intestine. These cells are particularly important because colon cancer begins when cells in this tissue undergo changes that allow them to grow uncontrollably.

The intestinal lining is constantly renewing itself. Older or damaged cells are replaced by new ones, making controlled cell division essential for keeping the digestive tract healthy. However, when the signals that regulate this process become disrupted, excessive growth can create opportunities for cancer to develop.

In mice without IgA, the researchers identified changes in gene activity associated with cell proliferation, the process through which cells divide and increase in number. Crucially, these changes appeared before any tumors became visible, suggesting that the antibody helps regulate an early step in cancer development.

"We assumed there must be some sort of receptor on the epithelial cells that was mediating this," Donaldson says.

The researchers suspected that IgA was interacting with a specific molecular structure on the surface of intestinal cells, allowing it to influence how those cells behaved.

Gabriella Lima dos Reis, the study's second author and a graduate student working in Gabriel Victora's laboratory, investigated a promising candidate called DMBT1.

DMBT1 is a receptor found on the surface of epithelial cells that can bind to IgA. Previous research had connected it to several types of cancer, but scientists had not established precisely how it functions in the development of colon tumors.

How Gut Bacteria and IgA Control Tumor Formation

Further experiments revealed that DMBT1 plays two very different roles depending on whether IgA is present.

When intestinal bacteria are present, DMBT1 activates signals that encourage epithelial cells to divide. This response is part of the normal activity of the intestinal lining, which must continually replace cells to maintain its protective barrier.

IgA helps keep that growth under control. When the antibody binds to DMBT1, it restrains the receptor's activity, effectively acting as a brake on cell proliferation.

Without IgA, however, DMBT1 signaling can continue without sufficient restraint. Intestinal cells then divide more rapidly than they should, increasing the likelihood that tumors will develop.

The researchers confirmed that this excessive growth depends on several interacting factors. When gut bacteria were absent, DMBT1 signaling was disabled, or normal amounts of IgA were available, epithelial cell division remained under control.

Together, these findings reveal how a common immune molecule helps maintain the delicate balance between necessary tissue renewal and potentially dangerous overgrowth.

"If IgA is missing, epithelial cells that are performing their normal function -- responding to bacteria by producing new cells -- can keep dividing unchecked, leading to cancer," Mucida says. "We think this homeostatic effect is IgA's main function. This was a big surprise."

Homeostasis refers to the body's ability to maintain stable, healthy conditions despite constant changes in its environment. In this case, IgA appears to support that balance by preventing normal intestinal cell renewal from becoming excessive.

A New Possibility for Preventing Colon Cancer

By identifying DMBT1's normal role in intestinal cells, the Rockefeller team has uncovered a potential target for future colon cancer prevention strategies.

Instead of waiting until a tumor develops and then attempting to destroy it, researchers may eventually be able to influence the biological signals that make tumors more likely to form.

"Based on the mechanism we discovered, perhaps we could influence epithelial cells to be less likely to develop into a tumor," Mucida says. "We know, for example, that having polyps increases your chances of getting colon cancer, so we think that there could be an opportunity to target this pathway after polyps are removed. Right now, there are no interventions available at that point."

Colon polyps are growths that develop along the inner lining of the large intestine. Although many are harmless, some can eventually become cancerous. Removing them during a colonoscopy can reduce cancer risk, but researchers are interested in finding additional ways to prevent future tumors from developing.

The newly identified IgA and DMBT1 pathway could offer one such opportunity, although additional research is needed to determine whether targeting it would be effective and safe in humans.

Could Beneficial Gut Bacteria Help Prevent Cancer?

The discovery also raises another intriguing possibility. Certain intestinal bacteria may actively help protect against cancer by influencing how epithelial cells behave or by encouraging the production of protective antibodies.

While much of the research into the gut microbiome and cancer has focused on harmful bacteria that promote tumor formation or accelerate cancer growth, some microbes may have the opposite effect.

"What is potentially even more exciting is that there is evidence that individual species of bacteria can have really specific effects on epithelial cells as well," Donaldson notes. "A lot of research has focused on bacteria that induce tumors or can exacerbate their growth, but we have some evidence that there are bacteria that could do the opposite, just as IgA does. To that end, perhaps we could develop a probiotic supplement that induces a protective IgA response. This is all very speculative, but it's one direction that we could look towards in the future."

Such an approach would aim to use beneficial microorganisms to stimulate the body's existing protective mechanisms rather than directly attacking cancer cells. However, the idea remains speculative, and the mouse experiments do not establish that taking IgA supplements or probiotics can prevent colon cancer in people.

For now, the findings provide a clearer picture of how the immune system and gut microbiome cooperate to maintain healthy intestinal tissue. They also suggest that some of the body's most important defenses against cancer may operate long before the disease becomes detectable.

Mucida adds, "Overall, there is a lot more to learn about how the dance between bacteria, antibodies, and epithelial cells in the gut works to maintain health."

#4175. Comparison Test: Audi SQ5 vs. BMW X3 vs. Genesis GV70 vs. Mercedes-AMG GLC

We audition four upscale SUVs for a role requiring maximum versatility.

From the November/December 2026 issue of Car and Driver.

The vehicles assembled here are not the starring members of their makers’ lineups. They aren’t built for lapping racetracks, crossing the Rubicon Trail, or carrying a crew of seven. Instead, compact luxury crossover SUVs, as their compound-modifier designation suggests, play multiple roles. As premium-brand offerings, there’s an expectation of luxury. As four-door utilities, they must accommodate passengers and cargo. And as the more sporting examples of their ilk, they should exhibit a degree of athleticism. Living at the intersection of a variety of vehicle types, they need to demonstrate versatility and range, rather than excel with a singular ability.

We could have made a wider casting call for this production, but to ensure that the chosen crossovers weren’t forgettable, we opted for the more muscular variants, the ones with a more potent optional engine. That dramatically narrowed the field of candidates.

See all results for new 2026 Audi SQ5 for sale near 1500

The Audi Q5 is a relatively fresh face, having just been redesigned for the 2025 model year. The SQ5 is the model that fit our bill, with its 362-hp turbocharged 3.0-liter V-6, seven-speed dual-clutch automatic, and sport-tuned adaptive air-spring suspension. The Prestige package ($5900) and Black Optic package ($1900) were the chief items pushing this crossover’s $66,795 base price to $76,370.

The BMW X3 is a seasoned player in this arena, and the M50 xDrive best met our criteria. The turbocharged 3.0-liter inline-six has bulked up and boasts 393 horsepower and a robust 428 pound-feet of torque. It’s paired with an eight-speed automatic, adaptive M suspension, M Sport brakes, and an M Sport rear differential. To the BMW’s $67,850 base price, our test example added a modest load of options, which included the Premium package ($2750) and the M Sport Professional package ($600). The result was the lowest as-tested price, at $72,050.

Where you find a BMW, you typically find a Mercedes. Here, that’s the GLC in its new-for-2027 AMG GLC53 guise. It brings an enhanced supercharged and turbocharged 3.0-liter inline-six that makes 443 horsepower, a nine-speed automatic, AMG Ride Control suspension with adaptive damping, and rear-axle steering. Its $71,350 base price soared to $85,920, inflated by extras that included the Pinnacle trim ($3900), the AMG Dynamic Plus package ($2000), and the Driver Assistance package ($1950).

The award-winning Genesis GV70, with multiple 10Best trophies on its mantel, was a natural to include. It arrives in 3.5T guise, powered by a 375-hp twin-turbocharged 3.5-liter V-6 paired with an eight-speed automatic. It surprised us by having the highest base price, at $72,045, but in Prestige Graphite trim, there was little more to add, resulting in an as-tested figure of $73,895.

See all results for new 2026 Audi SQ5 for sale near 1500

What about the many other hopefuls from Alfa Romeo, Cadillac, Lexus, Lincoln, Land Rover, and Volvo? Most were screened out due to insufficient horsepower below our 350-pony threshold, while dedicated hybrids and electrics were not invited. Casting is a cruel process.

Let’s face it; none of this quartet have movie-star looks. The GV70, though most familiar (the design dates from 2022), is still pleasing to our eyes. The GLC’s appearance doesn’t break much new ground, but its long hood and rakishly set-back greenhouse give it an aristocratic vibe. The Audi’s fresh sheetmetal somehow seems not so fresh, and also not so interesting; it was the hardest of the four to pick out in traffic. Then there’s the BMW. Like a celebrity who experiments with creative facial hair or a weird ’do, BMW periodically feels the need to challenge its fans by changing up its look. Unfortunately, that’s where the X3’s design now finds itself.

HIGHS: Comfortable seats, capable chassis, solid feature content. LOWS: Forgettable looks, cramped rear quarters, not really a standout anywhere. VERDICT: Plenty of ability but eschews the spotlight.

That change-for-change’s-sake mantra reaches full flower in the X3’s interior. The operation of the outboard air vents and the placement of their controls are just annoying, as are the haptic door-lock buttons. “What the hell is going on with the door panels?” asked associate news editor Jack Fitzgerald. The design aims to be more futuristic than luxurious, but BMW’s vision of tomorrow is somewhat dystopian. “There’s nothing I like about these design choices,” said managing testing editor David Beard, “not one thing.” Screens and lighting set the scene, the better to distract you from the cheap-looking materials. After dark, though, the offending bits recede, and the glowing mood lighting enhances the atmosphere. Space is not an issue. The back seat comfortably accommodates two, but the shape of the seatback makes it uncomfortable for three (although that’s probably a rare use case for this segment). Up front, some of us found the driver’s seat to be narrow, but it’s highly effective at holding you in place during cornering.

Look at the SQ5’s dash, and it’s more like an assemblage of screens than a coherent design—the tacked-on passenger’s display is part of the Prestige package. Our car’s red seats and suede door panels were enlivening elements, but the patterned black plastic trim would look downmarket even in an A3. The driver’s chair was deemed good for a variety of body types, and the adjustable-height center armrest ups the comfort quotient. The SQ5 was also one of two vehicles in this test with seat massagers (the Genesis was the other). Its back seat, though, was the hardest to access and the least comfortable once you fold yourself into place—a consequence of the SQ5’s shortest-in-test wheelbase.

The GLC53’s cabin looks richer than its German compatriots’, and this is one Mercedes model whose big screen isn’t larger than life. Whereas BMW tries pointlessly to reinvent the air vent, Mercedes shows what a quality execution looks like. This AMG steering wheel still has annoying touch-swipe pads, though. We also noticed that the bloated center console impinges on the driver’s kneeroom, and the inductive charging pad buried deep within made the Mercedes the car in which you’re most likely to leave your phone (it will warn you that you’ve left it inside). Finally, the GLC’s set-back cabin results in a smaller cargo hold than others here.

HIGHS: Lowest as-tested price, best fuel economy, just misses first place in most measures of performance. LOWS: Odd-duck appearance, off-putting interior, not so richly equipped. VERDICT: An SUV that dares you to like it.

The GV70’s interior is the most glam, even more so than the Mercedes’s. “Easily the nicest,” Beard said. “You notice it from the moment you sit down.” Partial credit goes to the nonboring color scheme—blue with splashes of bright red—but don’t discount the glossy carbon-fiber-weave trim, the bright stainless-steel finishes, the ovoid shapes, and the quality-feeling switchgear. We love the rotary controller for the infotainment, which feels like quality. Unfortunately, it also feels like, and is located just ahead of, the rotary shifter. That quibble aside, the user-friendly GV70 took top marks in ergonomics. The Genesis also boasts comfortable, though firm, front chairs, with bonus points for their extendable under-thigh support.

If it’s an action hero you’re seeking, look first to the Mercedes. It has the strongest résumé, with not just the most horsepower but also the most torque, at 443 pound-feet (472 with a 10-second overboost function), just shading the BMW. Though tasked with carrying the greatest mass (4669 pounds), the boosted inline-six shrugs that off, and the AMG races to 60 mph in a launch-controlled 3.7 seconds, or in 4.7 seconds from a rolling 5-mph street start. Both of these results are best in test. So, too, are the quarter-mile time of 12.2 seconds at 113 mph and, thanks to the optional AMG Dynamic Plus package, the top speed of 167 mph, should you have to outrun a hail of bullets from machine-gun-wielding bad guys. All of this was plenty evident from behind the wheel, where the Mercedes felt like it wanted to storm the autobahn.

The BMW, with its “fantastic powertrain” (Beard again), was just a beat behind. Commendably boasting the lowest curb weight of 4474 pounds, the X3 posted a 60-mph time of 4.0 seconds flat, with a street-start figure of 4.9 seconds, both second best among our foursome, as was its quarter-mile time. Exhaling through quad exhaust outlets, and piping the exhaust note through the audio system, the vocal straight-six sounds great when giving its all. “The grunt is always right there,” noted Buyer’s Guide associate editor Andrew Wendler, but if you somehow don’t trust the highly responsive transmission to deliver—or you just want a more theatrical experience—you can pull and hold the downshift paddle to trigger a 10-second Sport Boost mode. It puts the powertrain into its max-sport settings, although it had no measurable effect at the test track. It does call up a cool 10-second countdown graphic in the instrument cluster. “It reminded me of the Power Rangers activating,” Wendler said.

The Audi also has a potent powertrain that’s always ready to break into a run, although it doesn’t sound quite as good as the others when doing so. “The 90-degree V-6 doesn’t have much character,” opined Beard. Nevertheless, with 406 pound-feet of torque, the SQ5 scampers to 60 mph in 4.3 seconds, or 5.2 seconds from a rolling start. Its seven-speed was the only dual-clutch automatic here and had the expected snappy responses but almost none of the low-speed lurching behavior commonly found in such transmissions.

HIGHS: Bucks-up cabin that’s a pleasure to interact with, blissful ride, quiet cruising.LOWS: Slowest of the group, trails on the skidpad, eyebrow-raising base price.VERDICT: Not the hardest-charging but still undeniably endearing.

With the second-smallest stable of ponies at 375, along with a lowest-in-test 391 pound-feet of torque, the Genesis had noticeably less vigor than the Germans. That bore out at the track, where the GV70’s 60-mph time of 5.1 seconds was 0.8 second behind its nearest rival. The GV70 tied the Audi in 30-to-50-mph passing but otherwise brought up the rear in all acceleration tests. Still, the Genesis is hardly slow, and the V-6 makes the right noises when the virtual tach needle climbs. For the most part, fuel economy represents a bit part for these players, but the BMW’s 28 mpg in our hands bested the rest of the group and shaded the second-place Audi by 4 mpg. Meanwhile, the Genesis racked up the biggest bar tab, quaffing premium at a rate of 21 mpg.

Asked to show their softer side, the Mercedes and the BMW struggle. They remain firm even in the mellowest suspension modes, and any leftover compliance goes away if you switch into Sport. Of the BMW, Fitzgerald said, “The suspension really beats you up on this loop, especially in Sport.” The X3 suffered noticeable head toss on the more challenging secondary roads.

Driven over rumble strips or expansion joints, the SQ5 seemed a shade less solid than the others. We posited that it was the lightest car here; actually, the Audi is second to the BMW but only by 16 pounds.

HIGHS: Pavement-searing acceleration, faithful steering, loads of stick. LOWS: Stiff ride, tiresome road noise, budget-busting price. VERDICT: A hugely talented but sometimes annoying A-lister.

None of the Germans rode as well as the Genesis, which barely acknowledged broken pavement. Wendler praised it as “serene on the highway.” Furthering that impression, the GV70 was also the quietest by far, registering just 19 sones at 70 mph.

On the handling loop, the flip side for the GV70 was a bit more body lean in aggressive cornering, though that’s a trade-off many owners would be happy to make. Shod with Michelin Primacy Tour A/S tires, the GV70 didn’t have the grip of the other cars. It also turned in the longest stopping distance, although its firm pedal feel won plaudits, as did the SQ5’s.

The Audi hangs on in the corners—like the Mercedes, it wears Michelin Pilot Sport 4 SUV tires—but the steering doesn’t have much to say. We didn’t love the BMW’s steering either, but its handling chops are substantial even if its Pirelli P Zero All Season footwear placed it third in skid-pad grip with 0.85 g (a previous X3 M50 wearing Goodyear Eagle F1 summer rubber did 0.90 g). With four-wheel steering, the GLC53 turns in eagerly, and we also liked the distinct on-center accuracy. Furthermore, it turned in the best skid-pad numbers and shortest stopping distance.

Coolly capable though it may be, the BMW was hard to warm up to. It hit a lot of marks, and not just at the test track. Its potent powertrain also had the best fuel economy. The Bimmer had the lowest as-tested price, but the least money bought the least equipment, and no one was a fan of the interior—the design, the materials, or interacting with it.

The Audi had no glaring weaknesses—unless you were trying to climb into the back seat—but no scene-stealing moments either. The powertrain and the chassis are undeniably accomplished, but the SQ5 would shine brighter if Audi could recapture some of its design magic, both inside and out.

In this high-strung company, the Genesis was decidedly not the sportiest, but it should be sporty enough for most drivers. It’s easily the most comfortable, arguably the most luxurious, and just so pleasant to interact with. That was enough for second best overall, despite a last-place finish in most performance metrics.

The Mercedes ultimately stole the show after acing our track tests. The GLC53 was engaging and exciting. “This is a machine doing powerful stuff, and you’re part of it,” Wendler said. While we admired the SUV’s abilities, it was not free of irritants, with road noise, ride quality, and some ergonomic foibles trying our patience. Sharp-eyed accountants might also point out that the as-tested price was much higher than the others, but some $5K of that was costume jewelry such as black leather with red stitching, 21-inch AMG cross-spoke wheels, and the AMG Night package. All of those options could easily be shed without dimming the GLC53’s star power. And then there’s this truism: Great talent rarely comes cheap.

The update, available now on all platforms, is dubbed Terra’s Call. It adds a new region, Itzaland, to the game’s world. It also reshapes the rest of Miraland.

It wouldn’t be a dress-up game without a host of new fashion sets, and outfits, of course - and there's plenty here, both free and paid. The launch of the new update also kicks off several in-game events, including some that celebrate the game’s second anniversary, and Nikki’s birthday.

#4173. GTA 6: How to Find the Secret Satan Boss

Christian Bognar is a Contributor at DualShockers with over three years of experience covering the gaming industry. Since 2022, he has written guides and reviews for publications including DualShockers, CBR, Attack of the Fanboy, PC Invasion, and The Game Slayer. He holds a Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration

GTA 6 has a ton of secrets to find throughout the large map of Leonida. Some examples include the Kraken deep underwater, UFOs, and even a Mario and Luigi reference.

One of the coolest easter eggs in the game is the secret Satan boss fight. Not only is it a really trippy mission, but it also rewards the player with one of the best weapons in the game.

A conspiracy theorist, a waffle house and a toxic sewage chamber – here's how to finish The Final Flush in GTA 6 for a permanent stamina boost.

If you are looking to take down Satan himself, this guide explains everything you need to know. Here’s how to find the secret Satan boss fight in GTA 6.

To find the secret Satan boss in GTA 6, you must travel to the northern side of Port Gellhorn and visit the house with “Welcome to the Hellhole!” written on it. You can find the exact location of this house in the image of Port Gellhorn below.

When you arrive at this house, the garage will either be open or closed. The Satan boss fight event can only be triggered if the garage is open, so if it happens to be shut when you arrive, then you’ll have to come back another time. This event all comes down to RNG, but there are ways to increase your chances.

A new Grand Theft Auto 6 Easter Egg has been discovered that involves the player being trapped in a horrific Squid Game-style horror event.

First, the garage has a higher chance of being open late at night. For example, it was open for me around 10:00 PM, so I recommend only visiting the Hellhole house around this time.

Keep in mind that the event won’t trigger if you just wait outside the house. Instead, I recommend using the RydeMe app to fast travel to another location and back to the house multiple times until the garage opens. This worked for me after five attempts.

Once the garage finally opens, walk inside to find two men having some drinks. They will ask you if you want a beer, which you should grab from the cooler next to the couch.

For the next couple of minutes, make sure you don’t do anything to piss these guys off. You can talk to them, but don’t choose the “provoke” dialogue option or throw a bottle to mess up the event. Instead, wait patiently until their van arrives.

A new Grand Theft Auto 6 Easter Egg has been discovered, where a random NPC has seemingly discovered the game's biggest secret.

When the van arrives, the men will ask you to join them for their upcoming ritual. You should agree here and climb into the back of the van, which will then transport you to another location with a bonfire.

Next, get out of the van and make your way to the bonfire to celebrate with the two Satanists, and wait until they tell you to look into the fire. Once the prompt “look into the fire” pops up, hold down the button to do just that.

Looking into the fire will teleport you to hell, where you’ll have to fight a wave of Satan’s demons and Satan himself.

Satan is not very difficult to defeat, but the fight can be a bit confusing. What you want to do here is shoot the exploding enemies that are running toward you, which will turn Satan’s health bar red.

This is a brief guide that entails the location of the Fast and Furious green Eclipse in GTA 6.

Once the health bar is red, you want to shoot at Satan to drain his health. When the health bar turns back to black, you want to repeat the process and kill the surrounding enemies to turn the bar red again.

Doing this a few times will have Satan going down fairly quickly. Once you kill Satan, you will teleport back to the real world.

When players respawn back to the real world after fighting Satan in GTA 6, they will be granted a permanent health increase. Additionally, they’ll be able to claim the Hellspawn Cumshot 12 Shotgun next to the large throne.

This shotgun is extremely powerful and is one of the best guns I have found in the game so far, so I recommend equipping it for any upcoming missions you have.

The world of Grand Theft Auto is connected, and there are many connections between GTA 5 and the latest game in the series.

Like many games, Grand Theft Auto 6 is full of easter eggs for you to discover. These are some of the best Leonida has to offer.

#4171. Protein redesign boosts DNA insertion activity and reveals how molecular machinery selects targets

Genome engineering is exciting, given its vast potential to treat and even cure diseases, but it is still a largely uncharted biomedical innovation. Scientists at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital recently uncovered the mechanisms involved in precisely integrating DNA into a target genomic location using CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs). By studying type I-F3 CAST, the researchers unveiled structural findings that explain how this CAST family achieves successful DNA integration at precise target sites and offer insights for future genomic engineering approaches. The results were published in Nature.

Embark is clearly sick of Arc Raiders players exploiting the game's mechanics to push each other around, and clip through doors and walls.

A fresh Arc Raiders patch has arrived, bringing a host of new fixes to several exploits players have recently been relying on to do things they’re not supposed to, and bypass certain mechanics to get into areas without having to go through proper channels.

The patch is fairly small, and surprisingly doesn’t include any buffs or nerfs to anything in particular.

The list of notes for update 1.4.0 is compact, with a clear focus on addressing several exploits. The biggest one, of course, is the addition of “exploit mitigation mechanisms” to stop players from glitching through locked doors.

This fix applies to all maps, and it’s intended to address an issue whereby players would not bring the required keys to access those areas of the various maps. Locked rooms, if they can be unlocked, often hide a wealth of high-tier and rare loot.

But players have also been using similar exploits to clip through walls and access areas outside the playspace, allowing them to ambush enemy players and set up traps that would be impossible for others to detect.

The game’s recent patch, which was released exactly one week ago, mainly consisted of balance tweaks to some of the more popular weapons and mines. However, it also introduced a few fixes to prevent players from clipping through walls by using barricades.

While on the subject of being in places where you’re not supposed to, the patch blocked exterior access to the locked room inside Spaceport's Control Tower, making it only accessible from inside the tower.

1.4.0 also fixes an especially nasty exploit that allowed players to bring up their weapons much faster than normal by quickly swapping to the quick use menu. There’s a range of smaller fixes for lighting and texture bugs here, too, and you can read all about it in the full change log below:

#4169. Scientists discover a new type of depression that common antidepressants struggle to treat

A newly identified form of depression may help explain why some people struggle to find relief from commonly prescribed antidepressants. Researchers at the University of Sydney have discovered a subtype called "circadian depression," which appears to be closely connected to the body's internal biological clock.

The discovery emerged from an analysis of clinical and genetic information from more than 10,000 Australians with depression. Nearly one-quarter of the participants in the study, which focused on people with severe, recurrent or persistent depression, showed characteristics of this newly identified subtype.

Circadian depression is associated with the body's 24-hour internal clock, which helps regulate when we feel awake and when we feel sleepy. People with this form of depression tend to respond less favorably to common serotonin-based antidepressants. However, treatments that target the brain circuits involved in controlling circadian rhythms, including melatonin, melatonin-targeted antidepressants and light therapy, may offer more effective options.

Published in the British Journal of Psychiatry, the findings shed light on the genetic factors associated with this subtype and offer a possible explanation for why widely used medications such as SSRIs (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors) are less effective for some patients.

A Hidden Type of Depression Affecting Nearly One in Four Patients Studied

To investigate the biological differences between forms of depression, researchers examined information collected through the nationwide Australian Genetics of Depression Study. Their analysis included clinical histories and genetic data from more than 10,000 people who had experienced depression.

The researchers identified nearly 25 percent (2,604 participants) as having circadian depression. Several recognizable patterns distinguished these individuals from other people with depression.

Those with the circadian subtype were more likely to experience seasonal changes in their depression, sleep for longer periods when depressed, and wake up feeling exhausted despite spending more time in bed. They were also more likely to be night owls, meaning they naturally preferred staying awake late and waking later in the day.

The differences extended beyond sleep patterns. Depression often began earlier in life for these individuals, and their symptoms tended to be more severe (such as mania and higher levels of suicidal thoughts). Genetic analysis also revealed an increased predisposition to inflammatory and cardiovascular health problems, along with major neurodevelopmental disorders, including ADHD.

First author Dr. Emiliana Tonini from the University of Sydney's Brain and Mind Center said:

"Our research has identified circadian depression as a new subtype, affecting around a quarter of people in our study into those with severe, recurrent or persistent depression.

"Depression is not a uniform illness, and understanding the characteristics of different subtypes means that we can give people earlier access to treatments that will be most effective for them."

Why Common Antidepressants May Be Less Effective

One of the most important implications of the discovery involves how depression is treated.

Medications such as SSRIs and SNRIs (serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors) are generally among the first treatments offered to people diagnosed with depression. These drugs work by influencing chemical messengers in the brain that help regulate mood.

However, the researchers found that these medications tend to be less effective for people with circadian depression. Individuals with this subtype also experience more side effects, suggesting that conventional antidepressants may not be the best initial approach for everyone.

Because circadian depression is closely associated with the body's internal clock, therapies designed to influence that clock may be particularly useful. Light therapy, for example, uses controlled exposure to bright light to help regulate biological rhythms. Melatonin, a hormone involved in signaling when the body should prepare for sleep, and antidepressants that target melatonin pathways may also be relevant treatment options.

Co-senior author Dr. Jacob Crouse from the Brain and Mind Center explained:

"Because circadian depression is linked to people's internal body clock, treatments targeting the circadian rhythm, such as light therapy and melatonin, may be much more relevant, and clinicians should reach for these much earlier in people with this presentation.

"For those who find that antidepressants are not working for them, it is important to speak to your clinician for advice about your individual circumstances."

A New Approach Could Improve Depression Treatment in Young People

Recognizing circadian depression earlier could be especially important for younger patients, who may otherwise spend valuable time trying medications that are less suited to their particular form of depression.

Professor Ian Hickie, Co-Director of the Brain and Mind Centre and a clinical psychiatrist, warned that failing to identify this subtype in young people can contribute to unsuccessful early treatments and unnecessary side effects.

The findings highlight the importance of recognizing that depression is not a single, uniform condition. Different biological mechanisms may contribute to similar symptoms, meaning that treatments effective for one person may provide much less benefit to another.

By identifying patients whose depression is closely tied to circadian rhythms, clinicians may be able to offer more targeted treatments earlier rather than relying on the same initial medication approach for everyone.

"We really want young people to receive the most appropriate treatment early in their course of illness.

"Most young people will be offered SSRIs first up, but for at least a quarter there are better circadian-focused medical and behavioral options to help treat and manage their condition."

Materials provided by University of Sydney. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
