#4141. Respect Your Elders: The London to Brighton Car Tour, Michigan Style

We leave behind launch control and triple digits to experience slow thrills.

From the November/December 2026 issue of Car and Driver.

More than double that if you count New Londons. There are about 30 Brightons, which I think means there are somewhere around 700 ways one could set up a London-to-Brighton antique-car run. Which, of course, is a totally normal thing to plan, right?

Maybe a few of you with an interest in early automobiles recognize the combination of London and Brighton from the long-running English vintage-car meet that travels between those two cities every November. First run in 1896 by an intrepid group of early—very early—car enthusiasts, the Emancipation Run was held to mark one of the first increases in speed limits: from single digits (4 mph) to a downright scorching 14 mph.

The London-to-Brighton event, or, as it’s now known, the RM Sotheby’s London to Brighton Veteran Car Run, looks like fun, so we decided to have a go between our own London and Brighton in Michigan with some antique American cars.

See all results for used cars for sale near 220040

Several things lined up well. Our course between London Township and the cute main street of Brighton was 57 miles, which is a good parallel to the U.K.’s 97-km (60-mile) route. Plenty of tree-lined country lanes connect the towns, a benefit when organizing a road trip for vehicles whose max speed may be more than 14 mph but still lags behind modern highway pace. Most important, there’s a fantastic community of early-20th-century-car collectors in Michigan, so finding folks who were willing to take out their Fords, Oldsmobiles, Pullmans, and REOs was no problem.

What was a problem was finding a date. Every time I suggested a weekend, I’d get a flurry of texts and emails from the would-be participants. “So sorry,” said Mark Turner. “There’s a steam-car rally that weekend.” It might have also been Turner who couldn’t do another date because of a meet for vintage Bentleys. “I don’t know if I could do June 6th because we have an HCCA [Horseless Carriage Club of America] tour down in Georgia,” said Brent Terry, with apologies. Eventually, I just picked something and hoped a few of the crew would manage to fit it into their busy, brassy schedules.

An 1865 regulation required a flagger with a red warning cloth to walk ahead of any roadgoing mechanical vehicles and limited their max speed to just 4 mph on turnpikes and highways and 2 mph in cities, towns, and villages in the United Kingdom. The law was initially intended to apply to steam-powered road locomotives, which were growing in popularity in England and threatening traditional railways. As cars entered the chat, drivers chafed at the restrictions. An 1896 act of Parliament brought that speed limit up to 14 mph and was thus celebrated by English motoring clubs with a 60-mile rally, an annual tradition now under the 60-mile-long name of RM Sotheby’s London to Brighton Veteran Car Run.

See all results for used cars for sale near 220040

Michigan being Michigan, the day before our run brought pouring rain. It turns out vintage-car people are shockingly willing to brave weather. “I believe it rains a lot in England,” said Rick Lindner. So, we showed up, as did eight shining examples of the earliest entries in American motoring, from a 1904 Ford Model AC owned by Lindner to a late-model 1913 Buick Model 31 helmed by Larry and Joyce Schramm. On the Car and Driver side, we brought doughnuts, passengers, and a lot of questions about old cars.

After the third time I asked someone for the cubic-inch displacement of their engine, John Grace (who organizes his own vintage-car run in the fall and lent his 1911 Regal to teenage brothers Jonathan and Matthew Sinclair for our tour, and whose wife, Dorothy, once drove a Model T across America, making either one of the Graces very qualified to tell me what’s what in prewar car stuff) shook his head. He told me that while he can go look it up for me, owners of cars from this era don’t generally describe their engines in displacement. “We measure in horsepower,” he said. “I never hear anybody ask about cubic inches for early cars.”

It makes sense. In the modern era, cubic inches tend to reflect power output, but back in the days when a Curved Dash Oldsmobile might have a single jug measuring 95 cubic inches and making only four horsepower, it was more useful to announce your car’s 30 horsepower than, say, its 200 cubic inches.

Grace answered this, and all my other questions, with thoughtful enthusiasm, which is something I noticed about all the antique-car people I met that day.

“The older the cars, the nicer the people,” said Larry Schramm. For the hobby to have a future, he said, it needs younger people to ask questions and learn how to drive these cars. Plus, “we’re all in the same boat.” If your car isn’t the one broken on this run, it might be on the next.

Antique-car drives are a bit like off-roading; it’s best to go in pairs so someone can pick you up and get you to the finish. That happened to Ted O’Dell, when his 1913 Buick Model 31 started running a temperature. When I talked to him about it, he was unbothered. Breakdowns are just a part of the process, as they were when the cars were new. It’s historically accurate to get a flat tire.

Even though I’d invited people through different contacts, most of the participants knew one another. Many of these owners have multiple cars, maybe a big four-door for longer tours and a Model T for local runabouts. They loan one another parts and cars and smudgy business cards for the one place that still sells horsehair upholstery stuffing.

We all gathered in a parking lot across the street from Darana Dragway. The vehicle owners hunched over crank starters to coax engines into action amid a chorus of grunts and pops, both mechanical and human. Clouds of tire smoke drifted over from the drag-strip side as smooth-bodied race machines revved big V-8s to numbers that would reduce our two- and four-cylinders to steaming puddles of Babbitt. As an example of divergent evolution, it was stark, but a show of mutual interest implied that while the bodies and power outputs were different, there was a shared soul among us.

Once our great eight were puffing and clattering, we left the dragsters behind in our own clouds of smoke (oil, not tire). I rode in David Liepelt’s 1915 Model T Ford at the head of the line. For Liepelt and his T, this marks a return to C/D. They were the stars of our Model T versus Model S story back in February 2014, and Liepelt is still mad that then–tech director Don Sherman beat his Ford in a Tesla, so we let him lead the tour.

Liepelt set off at a pace that would have shaken the drivers of 1896. He was all limbs, pulling the throttle lever back to full acceleration, upping the spark advance, rocking the gear-selecting pedal into high, and adjusting his Ruckstell two-speed axle. It was like watching an octopus drive a car. I had to tell him to slow down to make sure we didn’t leave anyone behind. It’s impressive what 22 horsepower is capable of, and while acceleration wasn’t going to be the challenge, nobody in the early 1900s was much for a panic stop. “Not good, but better than nothing,” Liepelt said as he barreled through an Ann Arbor intersection. If we were braking, I wasn’t aware. A line in my notebook reads, “It’s a very specific thrill to be in a car you could fall out of.”

Thinking of joining the antiques road show? Here’s what to buy.

Affordability was a theme among the group, which may come as a surprise to people who’ve grown up hearing terms like “Brass Era” and “prewar” only in relation to megabuck Bugattis and Duesenbergs on concours lawns. Those cars still command big prices, but more common brands have come down as older owners die and pass on to their family a garage full of acetylene headlamps and wood-spoke wheels. Our group was unanimous in suggesting a Model T as a gateway drug, including lensman James Lipman, who is now on his second T purchase (the first is shown above).

“The Brass Era ones may be worth $15,000 to $20,000,” said T owner Brent Allen. “But you can pick up a running T for sometimes $7000, $8000 easily.” Learning to drive a Model T is a challenge, but Allen said that shouldn’t put anyone off. Other owners will be eager to teach you, and there are so many reproduction parts. If you have a frame and an engine block, you can build a whole car from catalogs.

That thrill was a recurring theme. It’s the caress of wind in your hair like the first time you rode a bicycle. It’s the nervy pleasure of sitting the canter on a horse. It’s the very real possibility that you’ll never be able to stop. In a world where most cars can hit 100 mph before the end of an on-ramp, it’s amazing how exciting 35 mph can be when it takes all your extremities and maybe one or two of your passenger’s to keep the vehicle out of the nearest hedge.

For Jonathan Sinclair, the youngest of our drivers at 16, learning on a vintage car ruined him for modern transportation. When he was told that he couldn’t take the driver’s test in the family Model T, his mom had to force him to do his remaining training hours in a newer car. “I don’t feel anything!” he complained. “After the involved process of driving an older car, you get in a modern car, and suddenly you don’t have to worry about anything. It feels odd.” He and his brother, Matthew, had been planning to bring their own project, a 1911 Brush, but then the Graces offered them the key to the Regal.

Our summer intern, Alayna Wilkening, joined the Sinclair brothers in the Regal, where she was given the job of watching the MotoMeter hood ornament for signs of overheating. Her official report was they experienced no difficulties aside from having to explain to multiple onlookers that the Regal was a Regal but not a Buick.

Behind them, senior news editor Caleb Miller was riding in luxurious and secure comfort, cushioned in the azure-blue cabin of Daniel Coffman’s 1910 Pullman. I noticed with no small amount of jealousy that he had a nice sturdy roof support bar to hold on to in the turns. His post-run report was that his desire to purchase a vehicle of this vintage has only increased with each exposure. He also rode back with Liepelt and declared the trip “probably the most exhilarating 53 mph I’ve ever experienced.”

Editor-in-chief Tony Quiroga was spared the terror of Liepelt’s sporty T, instead getting the full touring-car experience in Wes Raynard’s flashy red 1909 Oldsmobile Model X3, which cost about $2000 when it was new. “This is the only one known to still exist,” Raynard told me. A quick look at past auction prices shows that the cherry Olds changed hands earlier this year for $55,105, which is considerably more than its original purchase price but a downright bargain to own a one-of-one survivor.

“The ride is so smooth,” Quiroga told me at our rest stop. He looked mildly disappointed that things were going so well. “I was expecting the adventure to be more adventurous. All of these enthusiasts know their cars so well that they could tear down the entire thing and rebuild it on the side of the road. Only everything is working, and we’re ahead of schedule.”

Despite Quiroga’s desire for more chaos, the overall consensus was that the inaugural C/D London-to-Brighton (Michigan) was a great success, and the gang plans to do it again in 2027. Barring any conflicts with the steam-car rally.

Like a sleeper agent activated late in the game, Elana Scherr didn’t know her calling at a young age. Like many girls, she planned to be a vet-astronaut-artist, and came closest to that last one by attending UCLA art school. She painted images of cars, but did not own one. Elana reluctantly got a driver’s license at age 21 and discovered that she not only loved cars and wanted to drive them, but that other people loved cars and wanted to read about them, which meant somebody had to write about them. Since receiving activation codes, Elana has written for numerous car magazines and websites, covering classics, car culture, technology, motorsports, and new-car reviews. In 2020, she received a Best Feature award from the Motor Press Guild for the C/D story "A Drive through Classic Americana in a Polestar 2."  In 2023, her Car and Driver feature story "In Washington, D.C.'s Secret Carpool Cabal, It's a Daily Slug Fest" was awarded 1st place in the 16th Annual National Arts & Entertainment Journalism Awards by the Los Angeles Press Club.

The time has arrived for another Arc Raiders update, and Embark has certainly delivered. Today’s patch, version 1.6.0, is among the smallest the game has received so far, focusing almost exclusively on disabling map exploits.

Perhaps more important than the patch itself, however, is the announcement the developer made around it.

Starting off with patch 1.6.0, it takes out a particular zipline on Stella Montis, the game’s most recent addition ot the map roster. Some players used said zipline to get out of bounds, something the game has been battling on several of its maps.

On Blue Gate, the patch fixes a collision issue that allowed players to vault through a wall, and fall to their death. The map fixes continue with another on Spaceport Launch Tower, which takes out a gap in collision that players have been able to shoot through.

The last change in this update affects gameplay feel around Arc enemies. Certain materials in the game’s world weren’t blocking their vision - or fire - when they should have, and this has now been fixed.

Alongside today’s patch, Embark also announced that going forward, we’re going to see fewer patches for Arc Raiders. The game has been getting updates almost every Thursday since it launched in late October.

Now that most of the major problems have been fixed, the studio is shifting to a slower patching cadence. Critical fixes will still be issued as soon as they’re developed, but don’t expect a patch each week going forward.

Embark also revealed that patch releases and in-game store rotations will now occur on Tuesdays. You should also expect the next few weeks to be quiet, as members of the team go on holiday breaks.

But, before everyone goes away, the game is going to get one more big update. The last item on Arc Raiders’ roadmap, revealed in early November, is the Cold Snap event. This is on track for Tuesday, bringing some new content alongside a few other fixes.

#4138. Stanford scientists discover 3 hidden brain types behind ADHD and anxiety

A new Stanford Medicine-led study has identified three distinct biological brain types, known as biotypes, in children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), anxiety disorder or both conditions.

The findings could help unravel the complicated relationship between two of the most common childhood mental health disorders, which frequently share symptoms. Published recently in Nature Mental Health, the study reveals that each biotype involves disruptions in a different set of brain circuits.

By examining thousands of functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) scans, researchers identified three biological patterns associated with different groups of symptoms. These findings could eventually help doctors recognize ADHD and anxiety earlier, identify new targets for treatment, and determine which therapies are most likely to benefit individual patients.

"The high overlap between ADHD and anxiety actually hinders our understanding of the neurobiology underlying traditional, symptom-based diagnoses," said co-senior study author Yu Zhang, PhD, assistant professor of psychiatry and behavioral sciences.

Doctors currently rely on symptom checklists to diagnose ADHD and anxiety. However, Zhang explained that children diagnosed with either disorder frequently experience symptoms associated with the other.

Looking Beyond Traditional ADHD and Anxiety Diagnoses

Yong Jiao, PhD, a postdoctoral scholar at the University of Iowa, is the study's lead author. Zhang shares senior authorship with Jing Jiang, PhD, assistant professor of pediatric neurology at the University of Iowa.

"We wanted to know whether the biological differences among children with ADHD and anxiety follow the diagnostic labels used in the clinic," Zhang said.

The researchers found that the relationship was not so straightforward. Children diagnosed with ADHD, anxiety or both could belong to any of the three brain biotypes, although some biological patterns were more prevalent among children with particular diagnoses.

According to the researchers, identifying these underlying differences could add a valuable layer of biological information to existing diagnostic categories, benefiting both future research and clinical care.

AI Uncovers Hidden Patterns in Thousands of Brain Scans

The research team drew on data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study, an ongoing investigation of brain development involving more than 11,000 children across the United States. Participants were 9 or 10 years old when they entered the project.

The analysis included 3,508 children who already had a diagnosis of ADHD, anxiety or both when they enrolled, along with 693 children who initially had neither diagnosis but subsequently developed one or both conditions. Another 1,947 children who never received either diagnosis served as a control group.

All participants underwent fMRI brain scans and completed a series of cognitive and behavioral assessments. To independently validate their findings, the scientists examined brain scans from another 224 children participating in a separate research project called the Healthy Brain Network. Each child in this additional group had been diagnosed with ADHD or anxiety disorder.

The team developed an artificial intelligence model to investigate functional connectivity, which describes how different regions of the brain work together. By incorporating diagnostic information and behavioral test results, the model identified patterns of brain connectivity that were more pronounced in children with ADHD, anxiety or both compared with those who had neither condition.

Combining behavioral information with brain imaging data revealed two major dimensions of dysfunction associated with ADHD and anxiety: cognitive-behavioral dysfunction and emotion-attention dysfunction.

Each dimension involves a different network of brain regions. Different combinations of these disruptions produced three distinct biotypes, which the researchers named the externalizing-disinhibited biotype, the internalizing-distressed biotype and the mixed biotype.

Three Distinct Brain Types and Their Symptoms

The three biological categories were mutually exclusive (each child was in only one biotype), but none was limited to a particular traditional diagnosis.

Children belonging to the externalizing-disinhibited group tended to exhibit higher levels of impulsivity, hostility, defiance, aggression and rule-breaking behavior. ADHD diagnoses were more common among children in this group.

The internalizing-distressed group was characterized by greater feelings of guilt and tension, stronger perfectionist tendencies, and more symptoms associated with anxiety and depression. Children with this biological profile were more frequently diagnosed with anxiety disorders.

Those in the mixed group experienced more difficulties with attention, irritability and self-injury. Like children in the externalizing-disinhibited group, they were more likely to have an ADHD diagnosis.

Despite these tendencies, researchers found every combination of brain biotype and conventional diagnosis among the children they studied.

Brain Changes Could Reveal ADHD and Anxiety Before Diagnosis

One of the most surprising findings emerged when scientists examined brain scans taken from children who had not been diagnosed with ADHD or anxiety when they first entered the study.

The distinctive biological patterns were already detectable in their initial scans, even though the children did not receive a diagnosis of ADHD, anxiety or both until later.

"We think this means we may be able to use the biotypes as an early indicator of these conditions," Zhang said, noting that identifying these patterns before diagnosis was the most unexpected aspect of the research. "It could help us provide more timely intervention for these conditions and slow down or, we hope, even reverse their progression."

Toward More Personalized ADHD and Anxiety Treatments

Zhang does not expect the newly identified brain biotypes to replace conventional diagnoses based on symptoms. Instead, combining the two approaches could help clinicians select treatments that are better suited to individual children.

Finding an effective treatment for ADHD or anxiety currently involves considerable experimentation. Children may need to try several medications before discovering which one provides meaningful relief.

"When doctors prescribe a new medication, it can take quite a long time -- a couple of weeks or months -- to see a response," Zhang said. "If the first medication doesn't work, they switch to a different one"

This process can be lengthy, expensive and frustrating.

Zhang hopes future clinical trials will build on the team's findings by investigating how different treatments affect specific patterns of brain activity. Such studies could eventually help researchers determine which therapies are most effective for each of the three biotypes.

"We want to find biomarkers that can really inform the right treatment at the right time," he said.

Researchers involved in the study are affiliated with Stanford University's Wu Tsai Neurosciences Institute and the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI.

Additional contributors came from the University of Iowa, the University of Texas at Austin and the University of Pennsylvania Perelman School of Medicine.

The research received funding from the National Institutes of Health (grant numbers R01MH129694, R01MH136197, R01MH145082, R01MH140425, U24AA021697, R01DA057567, R37MH101495 and R01MH132784), the Eagles Autism Foundation, the Stanford Knight Initiative for Brain Resilience, the Rosenkranz Foundation, the Brain and Behavior Research Foundation, and the Effie and Wofford Cain Foundation.

#4137. Toyota’s Hyper Z Prototype Is So Extreme, It Has Aerodynamic Wings Instead of a Bed

Built as a nod to Thailand’s crazy pickup-truck customization scene, this one-off is maximum Hilux.

Even though Toyota’s Hilux pickup truck is not sold on this side of the Pacific, most people have a pretty good idea about what it represents. Thanks to the antics in Top Gear in which they were drowned, blown up, and even set on fire, the Hilux has a reputation for being rugged to the point of near indestructibility. What you don’t expect is for them to be fast.

Of course, things are completely different in Southeast Asia, especially in Thailand. There, a pickup truck isn’t just a rough-and-tumble tool for work, it’s also a canvas for personal expression. Thai customizers turn their trucks into insane builds that would rival anything you’d find at Daikoku Parking Area in Japan or on the floor in Vegas at SEMA.

See all results for used cars for sale near 09274-025

To put an exclamation point on the launch of its new Hilux Travo Z Edition, Toyota turned to its Australian design department. Said department reacted, to use the proper antipodean expression, by going off like a frog in a sock, building a Hilux that’s so crazy it’s not even really a pickup truck any more.

The Hyper Z prototype features massively wide bodywork that struggles to contain 325/35 series tires on 22-inch wheels, and more aerodynamic elements than a small regional airport. There’s a table-sized front splitter, a diffuser out back, ground effects tucked under the body, and a park bench of a wing out back.

Also out back, an X-shaped wing that occupies the entirety of the pickup truck’s bed. Planning a run to your local DIY center? Whatever you’re picking up better fit in the glovebox.

The standard Hilux Travo is powered by a 2.4-liter turbo-diesel engine good for 150 horsepower, but despite what looks like a huge Hilux-branded intercooler here, Toyota didn’t put any power numbers on the prototype. It’s more a love letter to Thailand’s custom truck culture, showing what can be done rather than what should be done.

Perhaps of more interest in a practical sense is how Toyota positions its Hilux in this market. Overseas, the truck is offered in both a high-floor and low-floor model, the latter riding low so that it is easier to load and unload for practical working conditions.

Conversely, in the U.S. market, pickups of all sizes have never been taller, which you’ll notice as soon as you need to load them up. Could Toyota successfully market a low-floor Tacoma model, one that’s a little easier to live with for commercial applications?

Either way, the Hyper Z Prototype is a cool way to shine a light on a slice of automotive culture that’s specific to a region. If you thought authentic Thai green curry was hot, just check out how spicy the country likes its pickup trucks.

#4136. 8 Things You Must Do Before Ending Chapter One in GTA 6

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

There is a lot that you can do in the first chapter of Grand Theft Auto 6. You can deep sea dive for treasure, hang out with friends, complete missions, set up for Lucia, and a lot more. However, some of this absolutely needs to be done before you hit the end of the first chapter.

After chapter one, everything in GTA 6 changes, and you don’t have the opportunity to get everything done that you might want to, so you want to be sure that you have a checklist and that you complete it before making your way to Vice City and starting bigger and better things.

Note: It is important to note that taking up Mattia’s offer will end the first chapter of the game. There will also be spoilers ahead about chapter one.

Jason and Lucia have a chance to be madly in love in the beginning of the game. If you prepare for Lucia to get out of prison, work on Jason’s appearance, and focus on how they interact with each other, it will build a solid foundation.

There is a hard reset that comes at the end of the first chapter, and for a while, Lucia will be on her own while Jason recovers. With that being said, it will take a bit of a toll on their relationship.

This means that if you raise it up very high in the beginning, you won’t need to worry about needing to rebuild it as much later in the game, saving you a bit of time later on.

Immediately after setting up your BuckMe account, you are told that you need to start saving money. The first goal in the game is to have a total savings of $5,000 stashed away. This is a pretty easy goal to hit, especially since there are a fair number of money-making opportunities in the first chapter.

You want to make sure that you hit this goal, as when the hard reset comes at the end of the chapter, you will lose everything except what is in your savings account.

As an added bonus, putting money away into your savings account will also raise your relationship, so it is a win-win situation. After you have everything saved up, the rest of your money is stuff you can play with.

Explore the money-making methods covered in this GTA 6 guide, from side activities and selling cars to store robberies and bank heists.

Now that you have saved up the necessary cash for your family savings account, you might have some money burning a hole in your pocket. It is time to go on a bit of a shopping spree.

As I said, you won’t be able to take this money with you into chapter two, so you will want to spend all of it. Buy some clothes, and definitely upgrade your weapons.

There is no point in upgrading your car, as you will lose this after chapter one. Instead, focus on increasing your wardrobe and upgrading your weapons as these will carry over into the next chapter.

There are some missions that you only have access to in the first chapter, and some of them belong to Shirley - Jason’s neighbor. She is a kind lady, and she will occasionally ask you to complete a few tasks.

These consist of getting her some alcohol, and stealing a mobility scooter from a lady nearby. They are fun short missions that you can complete within a few minutes, but they are worth doing because they are quite fun.

Don’t worry about the treasure hunting, as you will be able to come back to it later on. Only certain missions disappear after the first chapter.

A guide to all the story missions in GTA 6 including the chapters and the mission titles.

There’s tons of details in GTA 6, which means that there are a bunch of collectibles that you can find scattered about. Some of these collectibles are books and magazines, and several of them are found around Jason’s house.

Before you end chapter one, you will want to get the books around Jason’s house. These include one in the bedroom, two in the living room, a magazine on the back deck, and one in the shed. Each of these disappears after the first chapter.

Along with this, you will want to grab the sunglasses in Donny’s trailer. You will make your way over there during one of the missions in the first chapter, so you shouldn’t miss out on them, but make sure to pick them up while you have the chance.

If you have been focused on upgrading your weapons, gathering clothes, and putting money into your savings, then you will probably need some extra cash in the first chapter. Instead of searching for treasure, you should instead focus on completing the lost drug missions.

There are four lost drug missions around Key Lento and up to the Grassrivers. These are special missions that end up disappearing after chapter one ends, so you will not have the ability to go back and complete them later on.

Since this is the only time you have access to them, you may as well complete them for the extra cash and spend it on stuff that will help you later in the game.

While I have already established that buying weapons is important because they carry over, it is also important to grab the unique weapons that are obtainable early in the game. There are a couple weapons that you can find around the islands in Key Lento, and they will carry you in later parts of the game.

For instance, the Assassin Pistol can be found on a small dinghy on an island and it is great for completing missions stealthily in later parts of the game, and it has become one of my go-to weapons for staying hidden.

There is also a shotgun that you can find that is quite powerful. It gets outclassed by other unique weapons later on, but it is great to have in chapter two.

One thing that is nice about GTA 6 is that it gives you the option to manually save. This means that you can create save points at key points in the game so that you can return to them later on.

I highly recommend completing what you can in chapter one and then creating a save point right before you go to do the tourist trap mission, as this is the last mission of the chapter, and it is also the point of no return.

If you want to play the game over but don’t want to deal with the slower pacing of the first chapter, you can skip all of that with a save right before the chapter change.

#4134. Dually Noted: The Reasons Why Some Pickup Trucks and Vans Come with Dual Rear Wheels

Dually pickup trucks and vans may look tough, but these models have four rear wheels and tires for reasons that have nothing to do with vanity.

The term “dual rear wheels,” as applied to full-size pickup trucks and vans, raises as many questions as it answers. Namely, one: Don’t all vehicles have two rear wheels? Good work, detective. The dual part, however, refers to the number of rear wheels on each side. Confusing? Sure. But consider yourself a member of an elite club. Send away for your decoder ring now.

You’ll often see so-equipped vehicles referred to in official specs or on a build sheet as DRW, as opposed to single-rear-wheel (SRW) pickups and vans. Out in the real world, you’re likely to observe dually pickups towing big, heavy trailers, often using a gooseneck or fifth-wheel hitch.

DRW vans are usually the longest and tallest, used for both cargo and passenger hauling. Simply put, DRW vehicles are meant to handle big loads.

Automakers go the DRW route on configurations of their heavy-duty trucks and vans designed for hauling and/or towing heavy loads. Having those extra tires means more contact patch over which to distribute the weight. It’s the same basic principle that’s used on semi trucks—having 18 or so wheels spread across the semi tractor and its trailer allows the rig to carry literal tons.

See all results for used cars for sale near 10400

On dually trucks, the wider stance helps increase stability as well. You can think of the two extra wheels like outriggers, keeping the truck better planted in the face of crosswinds or in turns.

The main drawbacks of a dually setup are somewhat obvious. You have to worry about six tires instead of four, which in turn makes tire replacement more expensive. For dually trucks, the extra wheels sit outside the normal pickup-bed envelope, necessitating flared fenders to cover the extra rubber.

Maneuvering a big SRW truck or van is difficult enough. Predictably, the additional width of a DRW vehicle only adds to the challenge. It’s why many dually trucks end up with a blemish or two on at least one rear fender. The fenders of newer dually pickups are made from lighter-weight fiberglass instead of steel, so they’re less likely to bend and more prone to cracking when they meet a stationary object.

This isn’t the case with most dually full-size vans. So-equipped vans add their additional tires inboard, which eliminates the need for flared rear fenders. The consequence of this arrangement is a slight reduction in outright cargo space due to the wheel wells extending further into the cabin.

Ever wonder why the front wheels of a dually truck or van have a severe outward dish to them? It’s so that all the wheels match and are therefore interchangeable should you need to use the spare. This dished design allows the rear wheels on one side to mate up with each other, which enables the use of two rear tires on both sides of the vehicle.

See all results for used cars for sale near 10400

The need for a dually comes down to capability. DRWs may be necessary to comfortably pull a fully laden horse trailer, a giant camper, various types of farm equipment, or the crops they help sow and reap. To get an idea of how much more a dually can handle, an SRW heavy-duty truck may be rated for a little more than 20,000 pounds of trailer weight on a bumper-mounted hitch, while the DRW variant of the same basic truck with a gooseneck hitch can pull almost twice the weight.

The difference isn’t as great with dual-rear-wheel versus SRW vans, mostly because both use bumper-mounted hitches. A DRW van may be able to tow as much as 50 percent more weight than a comparable SRW version. With some vans, towing capacity actually goes down when you add two rear wheels. Why go the dually route, then? Because that extra rubber is advantageous to rear-end stability—particularly when a van’s loaded up at, or near, its maximum payload capacity.

Dually setups are available on heavy-duty versions of full-size pickups and some large vans. Those looking for a pickup truck with a bed can choose this setup on the Chevrolet Silverado HD, GMC Sierra HD, Ram HD, and Ford F-series Super Duty.

In the realm of enclosed passenger and cargo vans, only the Ford Transit and Mercedes-Benz Sprinter offer available DRW configurations. You’ll also often find DRWs in use on cutaway and chassis-cab versions of these trucks and vans, which are used in the aftermarket to build things such as box trucks, tow trucks, and RVs.

In some international markets, where full-size pickups are much less common, automakers produce DRW versions of their sub-full-size pickups.

As with any towing or hauling exercise, make sure you understand the limits of your specific vehicle before loading it up or hitching a trailer to the back. Consider what you’re likely to tow or haul when shopping for your workhorse, and follow the manufacturer’s guidance on loading so you stay safe and avoid putting too much strain on the vehicle.

Dually is a term used for a pickup truck or van with dual rear wheels (DRW).

A dually pickup truck or van has two wheels and tires on each side of its rear axle for a grand total of four rear wheels and tires.

You do not need a CDL to drive a full-size pickup truck or an enclosed cargo or passenger van with dual rear wheels (DRWs).

Pedants will note that even a rear-wheel-drive dually relies on its engine to power four wheels (the four back ones). In a technical sense, however, a rear-drive dually is a two-wheel-drive vehicle, since power is sent to the drive wheels via two axle shafts. Similarly, though a four-wheel-drive-equipped dually may power a total of six wheels, the engine’s power only reaches the drive wheels via a total of four axle shafts (two at each end).

#4131. Too much of this common nutrient could be accelerating blood vessel aging

Blood vessels naturally become less flexible with age, and certain diseases can accelerate this process. As blood vessels stiffen, the risk of cardiovascular disease and premature death increases.

One factor that can contribute to this damage is an excess of phosphate in the bloodstream. Although elevated blood phosphate (hyperphosphatemia) is relatively uncommon in the general population, it occurs much more frequently in people with chronic kidney disease (CKD), whose kidneys gradually lose their ability to filter waste from the blood.

Scientists at the University of Colorado Anschutz School of Medicine have identified a kidney protein that plays a critical role in regulating blood phosphate levels. The discovery could have particularly important implications for people living with CKD.

In a new study published in October 2026, the researchers found that a deficiency of this protein caused blood vessels to stiffen more rapidly and shortened lifespan in animal models. These effects were especially pronounced when the animals consumed a diet high in phosphate. Reducing phosphate intake helped alleviate some of the damage.

The findings point to a potential new target for medications and other therapies designed to maintain healthy phosphate levels. Such treatments could eventually help people with CKD improve their overall health and potentially live longer.

"Phosphate is really underestimated in terms of longevity in all mammals. The higher the concentration of phosphate in the blood, the shorter the lifespan," says Makoto Miyazaki, PhD, a research professor in the Division of Renal Diseases and Hypertension and the senior author of the new study.

How Excess Phosphate Accelerates Blood Vessel Aging

Phosphorus is an essential nutrient that helps build and maintain strong bones. It occurs naturally in a wide variety of whole foods, including meat, poultry, fish, whole grains, nuts, legumes, and dairy products, generally in the form of organic phosphate compounds. Food manufacturers also add phosphates to processed foods and beverages to improve flavor and extend shelf life.

Although phosphorus is necessary for good health, excessive levels in the blood (hyperphosphatemia) can trigger a series of damaging biological changes. Phosphate additives may be particularly concerning because the body absorbs them more rapidly and efficiently than the organic phosphates naturally present in whole foods.

Persistently elevated phosphate levels can cause smooth muscle cells within blood vessel walls to behave more like cells responsible for building bone. As a result, these cells begin depositing calcium phosphate crystals resembling those found in bones, causing the blood vessels to harden (or calcify).

Healthy blood vessels are flexible, allowing them to expand and contract in response to changing blood flow demands. Calcification compromises this flexibility, effectively accelerating vascular aging and potentially contributing to numerous age-related health problems throughout the body.

A Hidden Protein Helps Maintain Phosphate Balance

Under normal circumstances, the kidneys remove excess phosphate from the bloodstream before it reaches harmful levels. As CKD progresses, however, declining kidney function makes it increasingly difficult for the body to eliminate phosphate and other substances.

Maintaining the right amount of phosphate requires continuous adjustments. After the kidneys filter phosphate from the blood, a portion is eliminated through urine, while the remainder is returned to the circulation. A protein known as NPT2A is responsible for reabsorbing approximately 75% of the filtered phosphate, preventing the body from losing too much phosphorus.

When phosphate levels are already elevated, however, this recycling mechanism can become problematic. Miyazaki and his colleagues discovered that another protein, called TMEM174, acts as a natural brake on this process. By binding to NPT2A, it limits the amount of phosphate being reabsorbed into the bloodstream.

Protein Deficiency Shortens Lifespan in Animal Models

The latest findings highlight the importance of TMEM174 in maintaining healthy phosphate levels. Animals deficient in the protein struggled to regulate phosphate in their blood, experienced increased vascular calcification, and had significantly shorter lifespans.

"We don't fully understand how yet, but somehow TMEM174 is destabilizing NPT2A," says Miyazaki. "And without enough TMEM174, homeostasis is disrupted."

A deficiency of TMEM174 appears to result primarily from genetic factors rather than chronic kidney disease itself. However, the research suggests that people with CKD who also have insufficient levels of this protein could be particularly vulnerable to the harmful effects of excess phosphate.

A Potential New Target for Protecting Blood Vessels

Miyazaki hopes the discovery will lead to treatments that reduce the amount of excess phosphate the kidneys return to the bloodstream.

Dietary changes may provide some benefit, particularly by reducing consumption of fast food, deli meats, sodas, and other processed products that contain large amounts of phosphate. However, Miyazaki explains that managing phosphate levels through diet alone can be challenging, especially for people with CKD. Because phosphate is present in such a wide range of foods, avoiding it is virtually impossible.

In future research, Miyazaki plans to investigate these kidney proteins further, along with the hormones involved in maintaining the body's chemical balance. He also wants to better understand why calcium accumulation in blood vessels is so common among people with CKD.

For now, identifying the role of TMEM174 represents an important advance in understanding how the body regulates phosphate. It could also help lay the groundwork for new approaches to improving the health of people whose phosphate balance is disrupted.

"Scientists have been studying phosphate homeostasis for over 100 years, so to still find a new protein that regulates phosphate is kind of unique," says Miyazaki.

Panini America announced its partnership with Rockstar Games on November 24. The officially licensed set is called the GTA VI: Sports Trading Card Collection, and it'll be the first trading card collaboration between the two companies.

Rockstar has been selling GTA merchandise for years, but this particular collaboration reminds me of the sort of extras that used to come with physical copies of video games. The maps that came with older GTA titles, for instance, were something you could actually use while playing and keep long after you were done with the game.

Ironically, GTA 6's boxed edition doesn't even come with a game disc. So it's nice to see Rockstar making something physical that draws directly from the game rather than simply putting its logo on another piece of merchandise.

Rockstar could've easily gone with a conventional trading card set featuring Jason, Lucia, and other major characters. Instead, it's making replicas of things you might stumble across while taking a break from the story. I'd love to see Rockstar do something similar with other fictional brands from the series, like Sprunk or eCola.

Unfortunately, Panini hasn't announced an exact release date, pricing, or which countries the cards will be available in.

Depending on when the cards go on sale in December, they could make for a pretty good Christmas gift for a GTA fan.

Lord of Hatred may finally make good on the Mephisto arc of Diablo 4's campaign, which started in the original game and carried through Vessel of Hatred.

Very much when we expected it, Blizzard has officially revealed Diablo 4’s next major expansion at The Game Awards. Lord of Hatred delivers a new campaign that continues the mainline story, picking up from where Vessel of Hatred left off. Mephisto, the eponymous Lord of Hatred, has seemingly finally escaped imprisonment to rule over Sanctuary.

Lord of Hatred is the second Diablo 4 expansion, and it will be available on PC, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S on April 28.

It’s always a big deal when we get a new Diablo expansion, especially for a game as starved of fresh (major) content as Diablo 4 has been. But perhaps the biggest piece of news out of the Lord of Hatred reveal is that the expansion is bringing not one, but two new classes to the game.

The first of which is The Paladin, whereas the second is being kept under wraps. Even more surprising is that The Paladin is playable right now for anyone who pre-purchases the expansion. This is a well-timed shadow drop, especially given that Diablo 4’s latest season has just kicked off.

The expansion adds a new region to the world: Skovos, which is where the events of the new campaign will be taking place. This is the first time Skovos has been in a Diablo game. Lord of Hatred brings a decent number of major systems to Diablo 4. The endgame is getting a big overhaul, headlined by the new War Plans feature. Through this, you can effectively design your own endgame grind, creating challenges based on the activities you like and earning rewards along the way.

Endgame activities now also feature their own skill trees, which can be progressed through by creating War Plans for your character featuring each activity. The new endgame activity, Echoing Hatred, is something of horde mode where you must defend against unrelenting waves of enemies.

None of that matters without loot, of course, and the upcoming expansion is bringing back the Horadric Cube, and adding set bonuses using the Talisman system. The long-awaited and highly-requested Loot Filter is also coming to the game with the release of the expansion.

Beyond itemisation, each class’ skill tree will grow with new bonus skill variants. In fact, the entire skill system is being reworked for all classes - though details are a little sparse at the moment.

You can also expect the level cap to go up, which is very likely necessary to fit all the new skills and various systems. Blizzard offered a deep dive into the new Paladin class, which you see on the official blog.

#4125. Common sleep and anxiety drugs could be harming aging brains

Adults age 65 and older who have dementia or other cognitive disorders are particularly vulnerable to the harmful effects of medications used to treat anxiety, sleep disturbances, psychosis, and other conditions affecting the central nervous system.

Potential consequences include more emergency room visits, longer and more frequent hospital stays, declining mental health, and an increased risk of premature death.

New research from the University at Buffalo (UB) offers some encouraging news, however. Between 2011 and 2022, the proportion of older adults with cognitive disorders taking medications that could impair their cognitive function decreased significantly.

After analyzing data from 2,796 older adults with cognitive disorders who lived independently, researchers found that exposure to potentially inappropriate medications fell from 39.3% in 2011 to 29.3% in 2022.

"This is a population with some mental issues that relate to the central nervous system. These drugs also act on the central nervous system, so they can be too much for older adults if inappropriately used," says Haowen Hsu, PharmD, a postdoctoral fellow in the Department of Pharmacy Practice at the School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences and first author of the study, published in the Journal of the American Geriatrics Society.

Reducing the Risks of Common Prescription Drugs

Older adults who have spent years taking benzodiazepines such as Xanax for anxiety or sleep medications such as Ambien may benefit from a medically supervised reduction in dosage or gradual discontinuation. These medications can negatively affect cognitive function, balance, and coordination.

"A central word for patients in this age group is 'deprescribing,' which means, for example, removing inappropriate medications and decreasing the frequency or the dosage. In some cases, it means replacing the current medication with a milder alternative," Hsu says. "This is why it's so important for health care providers to work closely with community pharmacists and homecare nurses to optimize medication safety."

To identify potentially problematic drugs, the research team consulted the American Geriatrics Society's Beers Criteria, which identifies approximately 100 medications that may pose risks to older adults. The researchers then concentrated specifically on medications that could present additional dangers for people with diagnosed cognitive disorders.

Using data from the Medical Expenditure Panel Survey, the team examined a sample representing approximately 29.7 million older Americans with cognitive disorders over the period from 2011 to 2022. They compared individuals prescribed at least one potentially inappropriate medication with those who had not received any of these drugs.

Medication Safety Has Improved, but Risks Remain

Although the study did not examine what caused the decline in exposure to potentially harmful medications, Hsu points to growing awareness among researchers and clinicians over the past two decades. The gradual but sustained improvement may reflect broader advances in geriatric medicine and efforts to make prescription drug use safer.

"We were happy to see the percentages of harm decline over that 11-year period," he says. "However, one-third of our target population is still exposed to these harmful medications, which isn't good."

Older adults, even those without cognitive disorders, are particularly susceptible to harmful drug interactions and inappropriate prescriptions. In some cases, these complications can increase the risk of death. These dangers are a central focus of Team Alice, an ongoing interdisciplinary research initiative at the University at Buffalo dedicated to medication safety.

Team Alice takes its name from Alice Brennan, who died in 2009 following a prescription for a muscle relaxant identified as potentially inappropriate under the Beers Criteria. The prescribing error went unrecognized within the health care system, and Brennan died following six weeks of preventable complications.

Her daughter, Mary Brennan-Taylor, shared her mother's experience with University at Buffalo researchers in the hope of bringing about systemic changes that would spare other patients and families from similar harm.

Hsu began the new study shortly after joining the university's pharmacy school and Team Alice, where he works in the UB Patient Safety Learning Laboratory.

"This work extends a series of national analyses our group has published on potentially inappropriate medications, quality of life, and health care use in older adults," says David Jacobs, PharmD, PhD, associate professor of pharmacy practice and a principal investigator on Team Alice.

"It is especially important as older adults with cognitive disorders are the least able to tolerate medications that worsen memory or thinking, yet nearly one in three are still receiving them. Most of these patients have a regular source of care so these medications can be identified and addressed with their care team."

Improving Medication Safety for Older Adults

Other contributors to the study included Team Alice's fellow principal investigators Ranjit Singh, MD, associate professor and interim chair of the Department of Family Medicine at UB's Jacobs School of Medicine and Biomedical Sciences, and Robert Wahler, PharmD, clinical associate professor of pharmacy practice.

Collin Clark, PharmD, clinical associate professor of pharmacy practice, and Steven Feuerstein, an information systems analyst at the Jacobs School, also contributed to the research.

The findings underscore the value of thorough medication reviews during routine outpatient appointments. The researchers also suggest incorporating clinical assessment tools such as the Drug Burden Index into acute and outpatient care. Such tools can help health care professionals assess the combined effects of medications that act on the central nervous system and potentially prevent avoidable complications.

Further research is needed to establish whether improving medication use can enhance quality of life and reduce hospital admissions and emergency room visits among older adults experiencing cognitive difficulties.

A Rapidly Aging Population Raises New Concerns

The findings arrive at a significant moment in global demographic history. According to a recent report from the U.S. Census Bureau, adults age 65 and older now outnumber children from birth through age 5 worldwide for the first time in human history.

However, greater longevity does not necessarily translate into more years of good health. The same report indicates that nearly 75% of adults age 65 and older have at least two chronic health conditions. Managing multiple illnesses often requires taking more medications, some of which may have detrimental effects on the aging body and brain.

"This is an issue that has been building for decades, but the growth of the older adult population has arrived sooner than we expected," Hsu says. "This means that health care professionals need to pay closer attention than ever to medication safety, especially for older adults experiencing cognitive decline or other complex health concerns."

The Sentinels lineup for 2027 now reads johnqt, brawk, OXY, canezerra and keiko. Zellsis rounds out the group as sixth man. He came back to the organisation on 7 November in that role and as a content creator. Contract lengths were not disclosed.

Sentinels called keiko ‘bloody brilliant’ in its announcement. Riot’s VALORANT Esports account then shared the news and described him as ‘the finishing touch’ on the lineup.

Sheep Esports first reported the move on 8 November, citing sources, and said keiko was expected to play controller. The same report had brawk on initiator and johnqt on sentinel.

The signing ends a rapid rebuild. OXY arrived on 2 November and brawk a day later. canezerra followed on 6 November. Four days after that, cortezia and Reduxx were released.

Only a few hours before joining Sentinels, brawk had ruled out staying at NRG.

keiko’s NRG spell ran from 12 November 2025 to 21 October 2026. He finished third at Masters Santiago 2026. He also placed third in both VCT Americas Stage 1 and Stage 2. At Champions 2026 he finished joint fifth to sixth.

That spell ended once Champions was over. NRG told him he would not be kept for the following year, keiko said on X on 21 October. He was then free to look for a new team as a restricted free agent.

Sentinels reached no international event in 2026. The team went out of that year’s Kickoff in the bottom four. It then missed the playoffs in both Stage 1 and Stage 2. Adding a player with that run of results is consistent with a side trying to close the gap quickly.

keiko was born on 12 September 2003. He grew up in and around London. He played competitive Fortnite before switching to VALORANT. His VALORANT career began at UK sides WYLDE, from May to August 2022, and BONK, from October to December 2022. He then joined Apeks from January to November 2023. That year he won the Challengers Rising Stars award. Team Liquid followed, from November 2023 to November 2025. His move to Sentinels places a British player at the centre of a rebuilt Americas contender.

The final piece has arrived, and he's bloody brilliant@Keikofps is officially a Sentinel pic.twitter.com/F5plGsyugj

— Sentinels (@Sentinels) November 16, 2026

The new lineup’s next test is the Americas Kickoff. Partner teams are guaranteed a place only at Kickoff. The Americas has eight partner teams, and all of them receive direct invitations to its event. Four further places go to non-partner teams.

The 2027 Kickoff events will be played in person in each international region. One of the non-partner places in the Americas will be decided by a Last Chance Qualifier in São Paulo on 17–18 December.

#4123. Take-Two's GTA 6 PC Port Crackdown Has Already Taken Down Over 3,000 Repositories

Grand Theft Auto 6 is still a console exclusive, but some fans have already been trying to get it running on PC. Take-Two Interactive has filed a copyright complaint against Leonida, an unofficial port based on the Xbox Series version of the game. It's not just the original project that's been affected: GitHub has taken action against a whopping 3,007 repositories in response to the complaint.

According to a new rumor, Rockstar Games could release the GTA 6 PC port just a few months after the highly anticipated console launch.

Leonida was named after the fictional state in which GTA 6 takes place, and it was one of several attempts to get the console version running on a computer. Unlike some of the fan-made PC ports we've seen for older console games, though, this one was being developed using a build of a game that had only just come out.

In a DMCA notice published on GitHub on November 24, Take-Two's intellectual property enforcement team alleges that Leonida infringes upon the company's copyright and violates Rockstar's terms of service. The notice says an Xbox Series build of GTA 6 was leaked on November 20, with the Leonida repository appearing a day later.

The developers had asked users to supply their own game files, but Take-Two argues that the project was designed specifically to make use of the leaked build. The company requested that GitHub take down Leonida and its forks, arguing that the alleged infringement couldn't be addressed without disabling the repositories altogether.

GitHub says it acted on the entire network of 3,007 repositories. That number includes forks, which are essentially copies of a repository that other GitHub users can work on independently. That doesn't mean there were 3,007 different GTA 6 PC ports in development, though.

An Xbox Series build of GTA 6 was leaked on November 20, with the Leonida repository appearing a day later.

According to PC Gamer, the team appeared to have reached the game's splash screen during a livestream before it crashed. The project's lead developer, NotRexed, subsequently announced their departure, citing the loss of the Discord server as well as the pressure of managing the community alongside school and sports.

Take-Two's takedown hasn't put an end to Leonida, either. According to the same report, others have already tried to pick up where the original developer left off.

It's a familiar situation for those of us who primarily play on PC. GTA 4 came to PC several months after its console debut, while we had to wait more than a year and a half after GTA 5's original launch for its PC version. Even Red Dead Redemption 2 took roughly a year to make its way over.

The difference this time is that a report has suggested GTA 6 could arrive on PC in the first quarter of 2027. If that turns out to be true, the wait would be much shorter than it was for Rockstar's last two major releases. There hasn't been an official announcement confirming that release window, however.

Getting GTA 6 to boot on a PC and getting it to run well enough to play through the entire game are two very different things. Just look at how badly Rockstar handled GTA 4's PC port. Even hardware that far exceeded the game's original system requirements struggled to run it smoothly, and Rockstar never bothered to properly fix it.

Modders have spent years ironing out its performance issues and bugs, and while that's still an ongoing process, I'd argue 2026 has been the best year yet to play GTA 4 on PC. Even if one of these unofficial efforts eventually makes it past the splash screen, there's no telling how well the game will run on a typical gaming PC or whether it'll have major bugs throughout the story.

Hopefully, Rockstar won't keep us in the dark for too long regarding the official PC version. Even an approximate release window would be welcome at this point, especially for anyone holding off on buying a console just to play GTA 6.

#4122. Arc Raiders' Cold Snap update brings snow storms to most maps, new events and a new Raider Deck

Arc Raiders has delivered a big new update that's very fittingly on theme, and it's not without new mechanics.

Arc Raiders is kicking off its last major event of the year. The Cold Snap update arrives moments from now, and it’s perhaps the game’s biggest since its momentous launch in late October. We’ve known about the existence of Cold Snap for a while, of course, but we finally have a solid idea about what to expect.

Cold Snap is made up of different components - including new content - that all players have access to.

As the name suggests, of course, Cold Snap introduces the new snowfall Map Condition. As part of this, maps will be covered in snow, thanks to snowstorms sweeping across them. For one, snowfall makes it harder to see enemies, but it also turns all lakes solid.

There’s a new mechanic associated with this, and it’s actually similar to Battlefield 6’s Winter Offensive update. Staying outdoors for too long will cause you to catch frostbite, which slowly drains HP. Embark says you’re going to need to bring more healing items with you on raids, and it doesn’t look like there are firepits that could keep you warm - though staying indoors for a while will help.

Cold Snap arrives alongside limited-time events that will be available until Tuesday, January 13. The snowfall visual update and new frostbite mechanics are available on Dam Battlegrounds, Buried City, Spaceport, and The Blue Gate.

One of the new events is Flickering Flames, which comes with its own progression track of 25 levels. Content is, of course, unlocked using Merits, which are earned from XP in matches. The other event is the Candleberry Banquet Project, which requires you to donate items found on the surface (including Candleberries).

You’ll earn rewards each time, and each stage completed will reveal a new scene on the banquet table. Likewise, there are cosmetic rewards as part of each stage, and you can use it as a source of Merits, too.

While on the subject, the new update also kicks off a new Raider Deck (battle pass). Available from December 26, The Goalie Raider Deck is pretty much what you’d expect. You’ll find several pages of cosmetic and useful items. The new Deck will be available to all players for free.

#4121. Caedrel and Dan Gaskin win for Britain at Esports Awards as Counter-Strike 2 takes top game

Britain's Marc 'Caedrel' Lamont and Dan Gaskin were among the winners at the 2026 Esports Awards in Miami, where Counter-Strike 2 was named game of the year and Team Vitality and BLAST also took industry honours. The results crown a strong Counter-Strike year eight days before the next CS2 Major begins in Singapore.

The 2026 Esports Awards honoured two British figures from the streaming and broadcast side of the scene. Caedrel is a League of Legends streamer and co-streamer. Gaskin works as a caster.

The ceremony took place on the evening of 17 November at the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts of Miami-Dade County. It is the scene’s main end-of-season awards show. The event began in London in 2016.

At Worlds 2026, Caedrel was the top co-streamer for both hours watched and peak viewers, according to Esports Charts.

His co-stream success came in a softer year for the tournament overall. Worlds 2026 peaked at 3.98 million viewers, which was 41% lower than the previous year. Caedrel’s numbers show how much attention a single co-streamer can hold even when the event’s headline peak falls.

Gaskin was not the only caster honoured in Miami. The other broadcast honours went to Alex ‘Machine’ Richardson for Play-by-Play Caster of the Year, Iain Chambers for Host of the Year and Anthony ‘NAMELESS’ Wheeler for Analyst of the Year. iShowSpeed was named Streamer of the Year.

Counter-Strike featured prominently among the industry prizes. Vitality’s award as best organisation came alongside Esports PC Player of the Year for Mathieu ‘ZywOo’ Herbaut. OpTic Texas were named Esports Team of the Year.

BLAST, which stages many of its events in Europe, was named Esports Tournament Organiser of the Year.

Vitality’s results through the year back up their award. They beat Spirit to win IEM Rio 2026 on 19 April, giving them back-to-back ESL Grand Slam titles. ZywOo took his 31st career HLTV MVP award at that event.

#4120. Scientists discover a surprising twist in how the body burns calories

Unlike ordinary body fat, brown fat burns calories to generate heat, making it an attractive target for future obesity treatments. Researchers at the University of Basel and University Hospital Basel have now investigated whether medication can switch on this energy-burning tissue in humans. Their surprising findings suggest that harnessing brown fat with drugs may be more challenging than anticipated.

While white fat primarily serves as an energy reserve, brown adipose tissue uses energy to keep the body warm. People with more active brown fat also tend to be leaner and have better metabolic health.

Exposure to cold naturally activates brown fat, prompting scientists to search for medications that could mimic this response. A research team led by Professor Matthias Betz at the University of Basel and University Hospital Basel examined whether activating a specific receptor, known as the beta2 adrenergic receptor, could stimulate brown fat in humans. Their findings were published in the journal Cell Metabolism.

Drug Boosts Calorie Burning Without Clear Brown Fat Activation

To investigate, the researchers conducted two experiments involving 11 healthy volunteers. They compared the effects of mild cold exposure with those of fenoterol, a medication that stimulates beta2 adrenergic receptors. The scientists measured how much energy the participants expended and used PET/CT scans to monitor brown fat activity.

Both interventions caused the body to burn more energy. However, the scans revealed an important difference. Only cold exposure produced clear evidence of brown fat activation, with the tissue absorbing considerably more glucose than it did following fenoterol administration.

"We were surprised that energy expenditure increased strongly with fenoterol even though we could not detect a comparable activation of brown fat," says Betz. "Our study shows that an increase in energy expenditure does not automatically mean that brown fat has been activated."

Exactly where the additional energy is being consumed remains a mystery. The researchers suspect that fenoterol may increase energy consumption in other tissues, potentially including skeletal muscle or white fat.

Implications for Future Weight Loss Drugs

The findings also suggest that the biological mechanisms controlling brown fat in humans are more complex than previously thought. Analysis of human tissue indicates that fully activating brown fat may require the combined action of multiple receptors or biological signals rather than stimulating a single receptor.

Understanding these mechanisms could open new possibilities for treating obesity. Current weight loss medications work by reducing appetite. However, as people shed pounds, their bodies often compensate by burning fewer calories.

A treatment that simultaneously reduces appetite and increases calorie burning could help counteract this metabolic adaptation.

"Ideally, we could combine a reduction in appetite with an increase in energy expenditure," says Betz. "But first we need a better understanding of how brown adipose tissue is regulated."

Materials provided by University of Basel. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

#4119. Arc Raiders' latest patch adds two of the most requested features, but kills Cred hoarding

The last major Arc Raiders update of the year has arrived, bringing several big new features to the game, but not without some bad news.

Embark has just rolled out patch 1.7.0 for Arc Raiders players everywhere. This is a significant patch for the extraction shooter for a number of reasons, not least of which because it kicks off a series of events under the Cold Snap banner, which introduces a new conditions to the game’s maps.

Dig deeper into the patch notes, however, and you’ll find even more to get excited about, including features players have been asking for since the game’s first public test.

To start with, today’s update finally adds an option toggle aiming down sights. This is especially relevant for PC players, most of whom play shooters with an ADS toggle, rather than hold. Another often requested feature has been the ability to reset the game’s skill tree.

This is now available for the cost of 2,000 Coins per skill point. It goes without saying that you’re going to need a whole lot of money to reset the entire thing, but it’s a useful option to have when you want to alter your path.

The next change is one that’s going to ruffle a lot of feathers. Arc Raiders now has a soft Cred cap of 800. This is now clearly shown on your Wallet screen, and the developer said the cap is necessary to prevent players from using their accumulated Cred to unlock new Raider Decks immediately after release.

The good news is that this won’t affect the Cred you may already have, but going forward, 800 is the most you can hold at any point. You’ll also notice that Shani has more stuff for you to buy with Cred, in case you want another way to spend what you have.

Patch 1.7.0 also brings a few other additions - and makes some changes - that are worth highlighting. You can now customise your Raider Tool, which likely means we’re going to see Raider Tool cosmetics going forward.

Speaking of items, the Aphelion weapon blueprint has been moved to Stella Montis, so you won’t be able to get it from taking down the Matriarch. The Bettina, and Rattler have both seen some balance changes.

The Bettina’s durability will now degrade a lot slower per shot, making it take 26 magazines to fully deplete durability. The base magazine size has been increased to 22, and the reload time has been cut to 4.5 seconds. Embark says this should make the weapon more viable in PvP, while also allowing it to stand on its own without the need for players bring a secondary weapon.

As for the Rattler, the only change it gets is an increase to its magazine size from 10 to 12. The idea is to make it about as effective as a Stitcher or Kettle at close ranges when it comes to PvP encounters.

And, of course, it wouldn’t be a big Arc Raiders patch without some tweaks to the game’s Arc enemies. This time, the Shredder gets all the love. The menacing unit now moves faster, turns more sharply and doesn’t get knocked back as much when shot.

The Shredder’s head now has more health, too, meaning you won’t be able to shoot it off early and confuse it. In general, the Arc unit should be smarter, especially when navigating narrow spaces. Finally, the Shredder now activates faster upon detecting (and being attacked by) players.

Beyond that, the main menu has seen a few changes to highlight ongoing events, make certain announcements quieter, make it easier to track Raider Quests and more. There’s a lot more in this update, too, such as changes to footstep loudness, several tweaks to loot and the value of certain items, and more besides. You’ll find the full change log on the official website.
