While a portion of Deadlock's player base is busy getting ready to celebrate the holiday, Valve has released another massive patch with a unique Thanksgiving-themed twist. Acting as a follow-up to Deadlock's limited Halloween event, the newest update detailed on Deadlock's Steam Page brings countless balance changes, quality-of-life improvements, features, and some themed mechanics to get players into the holiday spirit.

One of the most notable features of the limited-time event is a series of massive parade floats right outside the window, leading all the way down Blue Lane and visible right after loading into Deadlock's lobby. Aside from being simple decorations, these balloons also introduce a new mechanic by dropping Turkey dinners that can be collected for a new buff.

While the parade doesn't do much to start, after three minutes, refreshing crates will spawn hanging beneath them that drop the Turkeys when destroyed, alongside the chance of dropping additional goodies like buff items or Souls.

After eating a Turkey, you'll immediately gain two stamina and the 30-second Stuffed buff, granting you 5 percent Bullet Resist, 5 percent Spirit Resist, and progressively healing you for a total of 90 health. 20 minutes into a match, the health increase jumps to 90 instantly, and 170 over the 30 seconds.

While Deadlock's newest hero might not have been first pick, she's already taking the internet by storm.

You don't just want to go around eating every Turkey you can, however, as eating another while you have the Overstuffed buff will disable sprinting and give you 60 percent stronger gravity.

While the limited-time event is certainly a fun change, especially considering its real-life counterpart of the Macy's parade got delayed, the real meat (pun intended) of the update comes from the patch notes that have now gone into effect, with a few of the following changes being some of the big highlights of the update:

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

GTA 6 has been shattering records since before it came out, becoming the top-rated game in the history of Metacritic before it had the biggest entertainment launch (by dollars) in history. Sony is now joining in that victory lap by sharing GTA 6 milestones as they pertain to PlayStation.

"More than 39 million unique players have experienced Jason and Lucia's story in Grand Theft Auto 6 on PlayStation 5," Sony content communications manager Tim Turi wrote in a blog post today. That is a staggering number, especially considering GTA 6 also launched on Xbox and will (eventually) hit PC.

But that's not a sales record—Rockstar still has a ways to go to surpass GTA 5's 230 million lifetime sales. What is unprecedented, at least for PlayStation, is GTA 6's concurrents over launch weekend.

"GTA 6 set a new record for the highest number of concurrent players for any game on PlayStation, surpassing previous records across multiplayer, free-to-play, and single-player titles," Turi said.

That's the wild one to me, because that means more people were playing GTA 6 at the same time on the largest console platform than Call of Duty, GTA 5, or even Fortnite has ever achieved. Turi didn't share the concurrent figure itself, which is too bad—Steam remains the only platform that hands out exact player data. If the figure is theoretically higher than some of the biggest concurrent peaks we know about on Steam, then it could've been as high as 3-4 million players.

On average, those 39 million PS5 players logged 17.4 hours over four days. Let's just say my hour count represents the higher end of that average, and I'm still less than halfway through the main story.

#4014. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.0 brings a new world, and a Fortnite collaboration

Honkai: Star Rail's next major update introduces a whole new planet to the RPG, and way more besides.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a big Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

The upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the big new world headlining Version 4.0.

Planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

The squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

The imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

The Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

Much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

As you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

Version 4.0 introduces two new 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

General Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

Her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

The other new arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

When you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

She also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

Version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

If you log in after launch, you’ll get 20 free pulls and a new free outfit for Ruan Mei. If you play while the Yao Guang fortune event is active, you could earn 1,600 Stellar Jades. You can also expect a free 5-Star character selector to arrive at some point after launch, giving you a free choice between popular (but admittedly a bit old for the meta these days) limited-banner characters Jing Yuan, Kafka, Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae, Jingliu, Sparkle, Acheron, and Aventurine.

Finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the new outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

If you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be announced at a later date.

The prayers of Final Fantasy old heads were finally answered this year with the release of Final Fantasy Resonance, a particularly retro-feeling entry in the franchise. Between the real-time battle system and 2.5D aesthetic, it's a throwback in the best way, and fans embraced it wholeheartedly, so much so, even the devs were surprised.

"I think the action-oriented and 3D Final Fantasy games are wonderful too," Keisuke Nakashima, producer on Resonance, told Game*Spark, as translated by Automaton. "But I was surprised to see just how many people, not only in Japan but overseas as well, are eager for the kind of Final Fantasy they remember from back in the day, with classic turn-based battles and pixel art."

I'm a member of said corner of the overall fandom. Much as I enjoyed the huge, sleek main entries, my heart yearns for games that look and feel like the SNES installments, but with contemporary flavor. That's what Resonance delivers.

"We figured it was something we ourselves would enjoy, and that there would be players out there who’d feel the same way," Nakashima adds. That's always a good starting point, and the devs figured correctly, although there was some concern over just how much it stood out amid the slate otherwise.

"I expected opinions on it might be divided," Hiroto Furuya, director of Resonance, commented in the same interview. "I think the fact that a game with such an unusual background has been embraced by so many people is a positive for the industry as a whole, and I’m personally very happy to see it."

You and I both. Fans of the long-running role-playing juggernaut have had plenty to enjoy the last while. Besides Resonance, Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth continued the trilogy's blockbuster redux of the classic game, and Final Fantasy Tactics: The Ivalice Chronicles resurrected a fan-favorite for modern systems.

Final Fantasy Resonance is itself a top-down remake of aspects of Final Fantasy Brave Exvius, a mobile game from 2015. I'm willing to bet most who checked out this version glossed over the original. It's probably safe to get moving on a follow-up that draws from further parts of the narrative in Exvius.

#4012. Make Room For GTAVI By Deleting Your PS5 Trophy Clips

Hard drive space is a premium commodity, and its value has never been more apparent than in the approximately two and a half days leading up to the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. The game is a whopping 209 GB, but thankfully you can purchase the game and preload it now – which you should do because who knows if the servers are going to be able to handle the strain of what is officially the most pre-ordered game ever on both PlayStation and Xbox platforms.

The easy (and likely necessary) answer is to delete the big games you aren't currently playing off your hard drive, but there is a cache of arguably unnecessary data on PlayStation 5 that might get you there before you have to make hard decisions.

You may have turned it off (Settings > Capture and Broadcasts > Captures > Trophies under the Auto-captures section > Save Trophy Videos under the Video Clips section > Change to None), which if that is the case, then I'm sorry. I can't help you. But the default setting which maybe you've never touched, is saving a lot of unnecessary video.

Every time you get a Trophy on PlayStation 5, it creates a short video clip that I bet you never have and never will watch. Here's how to delete all those videos fairly quickly to free up at least some space.

First up, go to the Media Gallery. The quickest way to do that is to press the screenshot button to the left of the touchpad, tap over to the most recent media capture on the left, press X, and then press the Go to Media Gallery button.

Next, go to the Trophies tab, go to the Sort and Filter option (the downward arrow with the three lines), and change Media Type to Video Clips.

After that, go back a few screens and go to the Select Multiple option (the overlapping squares with the check mark on it). Go ahead and press the Select All option, then press Delete, and then hold your breath and commit by pressing Delete again.

In taking screenshots to write this little article, I deleted 110 14-second clips. That's about 25 minutes of video footage, which ain't nothing. Maybe it will help you not delete that one game that you started three years ago that you are definitely going to get back to any day now.

#4011. Hollow Knight: Silksong’s Sherma Gets A Singing Plush

Now that GTA 6 is here, studios can start to assess the impact and figure out when they can get back to business as usual. For Team Cherry, that day is November 27, when it has promised to reveal more about its Hollow Knight: Silksong DLC, and it paired a reveal of a special Sherma plush with that announcement.

Hornet might be the hero in Silksong, but the award for most beloved character in the Hollow Knight sequel almost certainly goes to Sherma. You meet the optimistic little bug early on in your journey and bump into them frequently throughout. You know they’re nearby because of the catchy tune they’re always singing.

Out of the frying pan into the Sea of Sorrow fire.

Now you can hear that catchy tune everywhere you go, as not only has Sherma finally been turned into a plush, but that plush sings the same song that he sings to alert Hornet he is, once again, nearby.

The officially licensed Sherma plush was revealed by Fangamer, which has handled most of Silksong’s official merch. The reveal was coupled with a clip of the plush in action, and it appears that you have to squeeze Sherma’s head to make him start singing. Better than it activating whenever you’re nearby, like in the game. Sherma’s cute, but that might start to get annoying after a while.

Mario Wonder’s Talking Flower toy serves as evidence of that.

There is no pre-order period for Sherma’s singing plush. You can just go to Fangamer right now and buy it for $36. That presumably means it will be shipped right away, so the perfect holiday gift for the Hollow Knight fan in your life if you’re still trying to figure out what to buy them.

The Sherma plush is around nine inches tall, and even though the biggest takeaway is that it can sing to you, its other finer details should not be overlooked. The plush looks exactly like the character on which it's based, and is even holding the needle and chime he clinks together to play the tune that accompanies his song.

As for November 27’s Silksong stream, Team Cherry has promised multiple exciting announcements alongside an update on the sequel’s Sea of Sorrow expansion. There was hope that the DLC might be released before the end of 2026. Considering how little notice the studio wound up giving between the reveal of Silksong’s release date and that release date’s arrival, it is still entirely possible that Sea of Sorrow’s date gets revealed tomorrow, and that it will be here by some point in December.

#4010. Heartopia shows off My Little Pony collaboration, and there's a pre-launch event to hold you over

Heartopia’s My Little Pony collaboration is close, and the pre-launch event has already kicked off.

Heartopia has officially shared initial details about its first-ever collaboration event. The game, which launched a month ago to great success on mobile, as well as Steam on PC, has already been a staple among fans of Animal Crossing and The Sims.

Things are kicking into gear, it seems, because the game is already about to host its first collaboration event, and it is with My Little Pony.

The Heartopia X My Little Pony event officially begins on February 14, but a pre-launch login event is now live through the actual collaboration’s start. The limited-time event offers players sign-in puzzles every day that will unlock time-limited Exhibition Passes.

The first actual piece of My Little Pony-themed content can be yours if you complete all puzzles, as that gets you a limited edition costume for your pet, based on the show’s Spike. The event itself, which will be available until March 15, brings My Little Pony’s Tree of Harmony into the world of Heartopia.

The ponies need your help to Wield Elements of Harmony so they can reawaken the tree, and bring it back to Equestria. In gameplay terms, you’re going to want to perform daily sensing at the tree in order to earn three of the six Elements of Harmony: Honesty, Generosity, Loyalty, Kindness, Laughter, and Magic.

The more you do this, the more the tree’s Energy goes up, and the more rewards and resources you stand to earn. Even more time-limited Exhibition Passes, and Moonlight Crystals can be earned as you water the tree.

Badge Pull Tokens are your big reward, which is what you’re actually going to use to get the special Pony Series badges. You’ll earn ten time-limited Exhibition Passes each time you complete one of the three sets of Pony Series badges. Collect all three and you’ll earn Town Collaboration Series badges.

Heartopia is a free-to-play game, so you know there is a Gacha component to this event. Expect six non-replacement Gacha Pools that each map to one member of My Little Pony’s Mane Six. Within each pool, you’ll be able to earn five outfit pieces, and one vehicle.

If any of that sounds interesting, definitely log in now to play the pre-launch event, which should hold you over until the proper show kicks off Saturday. If you’re already enjoying Heartopia, you likely want to learn about Onsen Egg Promise locations, Fish locations, and Bug locations - all of which can be found at those links.

We also recently updated our guides on how to catch Frostspore fish - and if you’re into cooking, how to obtain every recipe and variant. If you haven’t already, definitely see if you missed any of these Heartopia codes, too.

US President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he personally "convinced" the Nvidia board to reinstate Jensen Huang.

Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO a little under two weeks ago after admitting to an extramarital affair with Alice Huang (no relation), who formerly controlled Singaporean tech company Megaspeed International and has been the subject of US national security concerns related to AI chip exports to China.

Following the admission, as well as reports of two other affairs with Nvidia employees, Huang resigned as Nvidia president, CEO, and board member. Last week, amid calls for Huang's return from tech CEOs and investors, the Nvidia board said firmly that it would not reinstate him.

Cue the It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia title card: The gang reinstated him. On Monday, the Nvidia board said that it had "voted unanimously" to bring Huang back after receiving "input from senior levels of the United States government." Nvidia shares shot up 31.48% during Monday's trading.

Trump has taken credit for the change of heart. "I made the deal," he told CNBC. The President also posted a congratulatory AI-generated image depicting Huang as himself surviving an attempted assassination while holding up a red bra victoriously.

The news of Huang's reinstatement prompted a flurry of responses from US congressmembers on Monday.

"President Trump's direct involvement with Nvidia’s decision to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang raises serious national security and corruption questions. We must investigate these actions," said California Democratic congressman Robert Garcia in a statement. "No president who has invested in a private company should be involved in their board decisions. Congress must come together in swift bipartisan action and demand answers immediately."

It hasn't just been Democrats criticizing Huang's reinstatement.

"Jensen Huang had multiple affairs including with subordinates and an alleged Chinese spy. His own board described his behavior as lacking 'candor,'" said Republican senator Pete Ricketts of Nebraska. "I've served on a public company board. His behavior does not support reinstatement."

"The risk of extortion by a Chinese asset who's been banned by Singapore is risk enough to not rehire Huang," said North Dakota Republican Kevin Cramer. "The worst part of this is what we may never know. Congress should immediately pass the strictest export controls possible. I hope it’s not too late."

Huang is set to testify before the US Senate next Thursday, December 3.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer has been one of 2026’s breakout titles, but much of the game’s praise stems from its exceptional roguelike single-player mode. If you want to race against human players, you can only do so online. Thankfully, for fans of couch multiplayer, that’s going to change.

Developer Fuse Games announced yesterday that local splitscreen multiplayer is coming to Star Wars: Galactic Racer early next year. The mode lets you race up to three other players on the same screen. Former Valve writer Chet Faliszek – the one behind the likes of Half-Life 2, Portal and its sequel, Team Fortress 2, Left 4 Dead, and even Counter-Strike: Global Offensive – thinks GTA 6 is great… because you choose how to play. A fact that's lost on players complaining about optional missions.

The new Grand Theft Auto is smashing records left, right, and center as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic and, as per Sony, the "biggest launch in PlayStation history" to date. However, there's still a vocal (minority, I'd like to think) group of players dismissing it as a game that forces some sort of agenda upon you. Faliszek covers this in his YouTube video on the "moral yellow paint," so to speak, of GTA 6.

According to the Valve veteran, there's no real reason for folks to complain about menial tasks like painting the house as Jason or buying flowers, even if "the game says you're getting some kind of points or… gives you this list."

While other games use yellow paint to give you set boundaries to stay within, in GTA 6 you can stray in whatever direction you'd like and play how you wish.

In Faliszek's case, that means, uh, "bringing back bodies" and filling the house with corpses. It's all just GTA, after all.

"Now, would I do that in normal life? Does that make me a horrible person? Maybe. Does that make me a psycho in the game? Who cares?" As he says, "This is Grand Theft Auto." So, go on and ditch the chores to commit mass murder (if you please, of course). The writer notes that, again, it's all part of the game's sandbox elements – and, on that point, part of what makes Grand Theft Auto 6 such a stand-out release.

In a separate short, Faliszek dubs GTA 6 "a masterpiece," saying, "it may be the greatest game ever made." He references other devs' criticism of Rockstar's new title – such as Warren Spector's, which argues he'd "rather have hundreds of games and full employment" – and dismisses it, reiterating that "it's an amazing game" and "incredible." I'm sure the freedom (to collect bodies, apparently) is a big reason why.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

So, share in Faliszek's sentiment here and don't box yourself in with any preconceived "yellow paint" in GTA 6 when you don't have to. Clean the house, shower, buy gifts… or wreak havoc in Vice City and kill everyone in sight. The choice is yours.

#4006. Nioh 3 is killing it on Steam with over double the series' highest concurrent player count

People seemingly haven't been able to stop playing Nioh 3 since the moment it came out, and everyone helped push the numbers to unprecedented heights for the series.

Nioh 3 has had a massive weekend on Steam, the type of launch you just don’t often see for Koei Tecmo games. Indeed, this has very clearly been a monumentous release for both the publisher, and developer Team Ninja.

It is also, quite visibly, the most popular Nioh release ever on PC, and it was impressive watching more and more players jump into the game over the weekend and push the numbers higher.

Nioh 3 came out swinging, breaking the series’ Steam concurrent player record immediately after lanch, with 42,822. Anyone keeping up with how well the game has been received, and how much it’s been anticipated by series fans and Soulslike players, would’ve told you that it was only the beginning.

Late on Friday, and several times on Saturday, the game continued achieving new records, setting new peak concurrent levels every couple of hours. It happened again on Sunday, when the game finally settled on its current 88,045 peak concurrent (via SteamDB).

That’s an incredibly healthy player base, but more than that, it’s more than double the previous record holder, Nioh 2, which peaked at 41,325 concurrent players in 2021. Steam players appear to be very happy with the game, too, with over 1,560 reviews and an overall Very Positive rating.

You should also consider changing these settings before you jump in, as it’s going to maker your life easier.
